  • Manchester United are not too good to go down and absolutely are in a relegation battle.
  • Getting heavily beaten away to Liverpool was not at all surprising to Manchester United fans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:45 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 14:03 EST, 27 November 2026.

Manchester United are not too good to go down and absolutely are in a relegation battle. They aren’t good, let’s start there.

Getting heavily beaten away to Liverpool was not at all surprising to Manchester United fans. If anything, many feared an even heavier scoreline.

According to recent reports, not since 1973-74 have Manchester United been relegated and on that occasion that rag-tag group had won three of its first 11 matches. This time around, the side Mauricio Pochettino has inherited has just one win to its name.

Former players and pundits believe that eventually, yes, United will get their act together and that relegation isn’t really something to be preoccupied with right now. Fools gold.

Chief executive Omar Berrada claimed with a straight face that the club is heading in the right direction only last week. As staggering a statement last Friday as it was by the time the final whistle sounded on Sunday. By that point, it was insulting.

Slumped in 19th and it will be 90 days since their last league win by the time they host Brentford at Old Trafford in a bid to stop the rot on Saturday, United’s problems are threatening to engulf Pochettino and his staff - even though they revealed positive signs in the battling draw in Lisbon on Wednesday.

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the stats that condemn this sorry United squad and why burying their heads in the hand at talk of a relegation battle is the last thing they can afford to do….

Manchester United are not too good to go down and absolutely are in a relegation battle.

Trust Manchester United to be top of the table for the very worst statistic, officially having the worst defence in Europe’s top five leagues.

Luis Suarez's late goal for Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday made it 36 goals conceded in total by United across all competitions, taking them ahead of Lens (35), Crystal Palace (34), Getafe (34) and Union Berlin (33).

It has been revealed that that’s a Lens side that conceded nine in one match in the Champions League. That’s an Union Berlin side who has conceded five or more goals three times already this campaign, including a 7-0 drubbing at the hands of Bayern Munich.

Individually and collectively United lack any sort of structure, any sort of desire to do the basics, any sort of solidity that will have opposition forwards thinking twice.

Open it up to the top four leagues in England and United are one of only two teams yet to manage a single league clean sheet this season, with fellow Premier League outfit Ipswich Town. League Two side Barnet was on that list until they kept their first clean sheet of the season against Crawley on Tuesday.

Specifically in the Premier League, United rank 19th for Big Chances Against (22.2), rank 19th for Expected Goals Against (xGA). They have the sixth-worst Expected Goals differential in the league.

The Red Devils have the worst defence in Europe’s top five leagues, conceding 36 goals so far.

Matthijs de Ligt looked all at sea in his first league start in 357 days away to Liverpool to the point whereby Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher stated they ‘felt sorry’ for him. Leny Yoro continues to make costly mistakes. Diogo Dalot no longer looks up to the level. Noussair Mazraoui has regressed massively. Patrick Dorgu looks uncomfortable defending. Harry Maguire lacks recovery pace to go toe-to-toe with top defenders. Ayden Heaven is raw. Lisandro Martinez is a shadow of the best version previously seen at United. And Luke Shaw is injured.

It a defence that is majorly short on quality, discipline and leadership and that’s underscored by the amount of times they concede in bunches.

United shipped two goals in eight minutes away to Como and conceded two in five minutes a few days later against Bournemouth.

Twice in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa they conceded in bunches with two first half goals in three minutes, followed up by two Villa goals in five minutes in the second.

Add in the two goals in six minutes at home against Roma – a game where the attack bailed out the defence in a 3-2 win – and the two goals shipped at Anfield in three minutes against Liverpool, this United rearguard is not fit for purpose.

Put these defenders in a neutral kit and unanimously they’d be seen as relegation candidates.

Mauricio Pochettino must sort out Manchester United's leaky defence as a top priority.

That’s what set pieces are to United, a complete disaster.

Poor sides in the Premier League often must hang their hats on scoring timely goals and grinding out vital wins through the means of set-pieces.

United do not look capable of doing that.

In the Premier League, they are joint-20th for set-piece goals conceded so far this season with seven, while they rank 19th for set-piece goals scored (1). Only Nottingham Forest (0) are performing worse in this area than United.

Set-piece xG places United 19th in the league with 2.6, only marginally ahead of Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich Town, who are 20th with a set-piece xG of 1.6.

Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic hinted after the opening weekend’s 2-0 win over United that the Red Devils are easy to prepare for when it comes to set pieces, the area which created both goals.

Last season United ranked second, only behind champions Arsenal, for set-piece goals scored and 11th for set-piece goals conceded.

Pochettino took glitch with Chelsea’s hierarchy when they went over his head to appoint a dedicated set-piece coach and there is no suggestion one such guru is heading United’s way.

But make no bones about it, United have regressed massively in this area and it’s a slide without an easy fix.

Luis Suarez capitalises on Senne Lammens' error to equalise for Sporting Lisbon late on.

One of the biggest concerns right now is the ease at which teams are cutting United open.

Bournemouth are a very good team but their win at Old Trafford looked like a training game at times.

Sources indicate that against Villa, John McGinn strolled through the game, even if they went on to draw 4-4. There are too many examples of this.

At 111.5km on average per game, United rank 19th in the league for distance covered per match, with only Sunday’s victors Liverpool clocking in further ground coverage.

Worse than that, United badly lack pace and athleticism in the middle of the park as well as in wide areas. Where Liverpool fans marvel at the likes of Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola, United have built a squad severely lacking pace in all areas.

In a recent development, bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha are better inside and lack blistering pace. Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw have both been exposed defensively for pace this season. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are technically very good operators but both lack athleticism and are therefore losing the midfield battle too often.

Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick scoffed at the fixation on running stats before he was sacked and there is some merit to it not being the be-all-and-end-all – look at Liverpool.

But only Aston Villa (10) have been outrun by opponents more through the opening 11 games than United (9) and that, factored in with a porous defence and a soft underbelly at set pieces has United out there like a lamb for slaughter a lot of the time.

The appointment of Sam Wilson as first-team fitness coach, a move agreed long in advance of Pochettino’s hiring, from Arsenal will look to address the serious levels of underperformance in this area.

But with so little time on the training pitch and free moments in the schedule to fix months of fitness regression, it’s a gargantuan task.

Man United badly lack pace and athleticism in the middle of the park as well as in wide areas.

BELIEF (AND TIME!) IN SHORT SUPPLY.

As Pochettino had his head in his hands at Anfield he’d have been forgiven for wondering just how he was actually going to stop this sinking ship from fully going under.

He was back at Carrington at 6:30am on Monday morning staring at a schedule that promises 10 games in 39 days.

Players were back in for recovery sessions on Monday and training on Tuesday ahead of flying to Lisbon to face Sporting on Wednesday. Despite picking up a first point under Pochettino, there were plenty of individual errors in the 2-2 draw, namely with Senne Lammens conceding a needless penalty and later gifting Sporting an equaliser after failing to gather the ball in the air.

With recovery on Thursday, it means there is only time for a light Friday session pre-Brentford on Saturday, when it will have been 90 days since United’s last league win.

For all of the reasons outlined above, United are like a boxer on the ropes that is just trying to hang in there for the remainder of the year as the blows keep raining down.

According to recent reports, there are problems aplenty in defence and athleticism is one of the biggest worries. But mentality and belief is what Pochettino and his staff need to inspire as soon as possible.

With a busy schedule of games, Pochettino and his coaching team don't have time on their side.

United are the only team in the Premier League not to win a single game across the last seven, while they are one of only two teams in the 92 in the Football League to have just one domestic win this season, along with Burnley.

According to recent reports, having fallen behind eight times in the league, United have gone on to win just once, beating Ipswich Town. That was the anomaly.

From winning positions, they rank 19th for points won, taking just six points from the four games in which they held the lead.

And, ultimately, what are United’s players and fans clinging to?

Sources indicate that they rank 17th for home form and 19th away from home, where they have scored just four goals, while they are 18th in the league for shot conversion (5%) having taken the most shots (280) in the league. Only Sunderland and Nottingham Forest are more wasteful.

United still have to travel to Newcastle United and Arsenal before the year is out, both daunting trips for sides low on confidence, while Champions League hopes hang in the balance against Sporting and RB Leipzig.

Pochettino has a list as long as his arm with what he needs to fix but he has to get players believing again. It’s November and things are bad now, but they cannot throw in the towel when the going gets tough.

At this stage, indications are that the budget to be afforded to Pochettino in January will be ‘modest’ and is not set to be the splurge United likely need it to be.

Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins are on a list of targets, while Jarrad Branthwaite has been admired for a long time, albeit would be a player who would prove very expensive to get out of Everton mid-season.

United need to add at least two high-quality defenders in January, if not three, to give them a chance of salvaging a season that is threatening to get away from them.

The likes of Maguire, De Ligt, Dalot and Mazraoui are not suddenly going to improve and while there is a belief among former players that they won’t go down and it’s not a conversation to be had, those upstairs, who have failed miserably to date, cannot afford to show the same level of flippancy in what is set to be the most critical transfer window in decades for United.

Get it wrong and they could run out of road come May.

Indications are that the budget to be afforded to Pochettino by Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left) and Omar Berrada (right) in January will be ‘modest’, despite Manchester United needing reinforcements.

It raised alarm last Sunday night when it was pointed out that Tottenham Hotspur, who finished 17th and survived by the skin of their teeth last season, had 18 points after 11 games last season, 10 points more than United right now have.

In fact, since 2019-20, 20 different teams have had eight or fewer points after 11 Premier League games and 14 have gone down.

Two seasons ago both Crystal Palace and Wolverhampton Wanderers sat with fewer points than United after 11 games and both survived comfortably.

But the general trend is those there now will be there when all is said and done.

Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.
  • The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.
  • The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.

The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.

The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

Yet, after the first two days of trading, Anthropic stock closed Friday more than 20% below its opening price at $87.80, suggesting the hype had run ahead of what investors were willing to pay.

Anthropic's public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

2026 was meant to be the year Wall Street’s trillion-dollar bet on what US President Donald Trump calls superintelligence (SI) started paying off.

In the first half of the year, it did. Many AI stocks hit record highs as US hyperscalers like Google's Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft recorded bumper earnings.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The second half of 2026, however, has brought a lot more uncertainty.

While the stock of chipmaker Nvidia pushed even higher last month, many hyperscalers and chip or memory firms have seen erratic movements in their stock prices.

Then, after the Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, technology stocks sold off again dramatically.

The Magnificent Seven — including Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla — lost more than $1 trillion in value in a single trading day.

In a further twist, the AI sector took another hit last week as Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% over two days.

The sell-off followed revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

Huang resigned from the chipmaker, sending Nvidia's shares lower still and prompting a campaign by current and former staffers, investors and other key figures in Silicon Valley to have him reinstated.

"Is this the best timing?" asked Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at the Canada-based Stock Trader Network, in an interview with DW last week.

Dick stated Anthropic's valuation depends on whether it can deliver on a forecast by Goldman Sachs of more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030.

"If you get to a organization with $600 billion in revenue, [a] $1.3 trillion [valuation] doesn’t sound that bad," he told DW. "But when you’re talking about a company with at the moment $52 billion in revenue, it sounds like it’s overvalued.".

Other analysts, like Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings, are more bullish about the Claude maker's prospects.

Recent findings suggest that "Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation firm," Seth told Bloomberg last week, noting how it has grown rapidly and has strong institutional backing. "Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilize.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Wall Street is growing increasingly cautious about the sheer size of the AI outlay, amid warnings that future earnings may not justify the huge spending.

In September, investment bank Goldman Sachs estimated that hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their spending, leaving a gap of roughly $230 billion.

"We're not in Kansas anymore," Dick quipped, borrowing a line from the classic movie "The Wizard of Oz," which means times have changed. Now, he said, investors are telling companies: "Show me the money.".

Other analysts, however, think it's too soon to expect the AI bubble to burst, including Kit Rees, investment strategist at London-based wealth manager Quilter, who thinks the post-election rout was a "healthy correction.".

Recent findings suggest that "We’re still in the very early innings of the AI build-out," Rees told DW. "There’s still a lot of excitement around this technology and investors will want to have a slice of the pie.".

In addition to the roughly $800 billion invested in capital expenditures this year, AI hyperscalers proposal to spend a further $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

Industry observers note that with many investors already running for the hills, Rees isn’t convinced the AI bubble will burst in the way skeptics expect. She thinks they should watch for stronger signs that the AI trade is maturing.

This could be "a slowdown in AI-related revenues for companies, or signs of less demand or less appetite for financing companies’ AI plans, be it through debt or through equity offerings," Rees told DW.

There are early signs that investors have less appetite for AI-related debt. Borrowing costs for AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave and Oracle have soared recently. Even the cost of insuring Nvidia’s debt against default has risen 76% in a month, CNBC reported recently.

"They [Oracle] have been spending, some people say, like drunken sailors," Dick told DW. "They’ve compromised their balance sheet to a point where the stock’s fallen 65% from the highs.".

It has been revealed that that has not stopped Oracle, along with Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet, from continuing to issue upcoming AI bonds. Since the end of last month, the four AI giants have announced deals worth $67 billion.

Rees stated another sign could be any upcoming regulations that make it harder to build out US data centers, due to pressure on local water and electricity supplies.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In his upcoming book "AI Mania: Blather, Bluster, and the Bubble of All Bubbles," economist Gary Smith compares the AI boom with earlier frenzies around railways, automobiles, television and the internet. He warns of a "frightful crash" when the AI bubble eventually pops.

Recent findings suggest that when the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market index lost nearly 80% of its value. Yet, previous bubbles have often lasted far longer than expected, making the timing of any crash hard to predict.

Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at UK-based investment bank Panmure Liberum, believes a reckoning could happen as early as next year.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement told Bloomberg last month.

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

According to recent reports, roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Sources indicate that even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage remarked. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

According to recent reports, it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be remarked of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

Sources indicate that it was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that everton has confirmed a fresh multi-year partnership with WTW, a leading global advisory, broking and solutions manufacturer, as the Club continues to expand its commercial portfolio into new categories. The agreement sees WTW become Everton’s ‘Official Insurance Partner’, bringing specialist expertise in insurance, risk management and analytics to support the Club’s operations and long-term ambitions. Operating across more than 140 countries and markets, WTW becomes the latest internationally-recognised business to join Everton’s growing partnership portfolio, following recent agreements with NOCO, Nestlé and JYSK. Through the agreement, WTW will benefit from brand visibility at Hill Dickinson Stadium and across Everton’s digital and social media channels as well as commercial activation opportunities through access to the Club’s waterfront home for client hospitality, business events and engagement activities. The agreement allows for wider collaboration, including community initiatives, that will also be explored. As Everton’s exclusive partner in the insurance brokerage category, WTW will also provide tailored risk and insurance advice and solutions, drawing on its global insurance-market relationships and extensive experience across the sports and entertainment industry. Adriano Galliani has hit back at Giovanni Malagò, claiming Juventus, Inter and Milan are among the Serie A clubs who have switched sides in the race for the FIGC presidency.

With quotes via La Gazzetta dello Sport, the two candidates traded light-hearted jabs on Thursday, with the election now just over two weeks away.

Speaking on the sidelines of a CONI council meeting, Malagò suggested he wouldn’t have run in Galliani’s position. He pointed to the U-turn made by the “technical components”, meaning the players’ union (AIC) and the coaches’ association (AIAC).

“What would I have done in Galliani’s place? Honestly, I wouldn’t have stood, given the U-turn by the technical components,” Malagò said. “But Adriano is a friend, and I’ll never say anything that isn’t affectionate. So I say it with a smile, even if I think this view is widely shared.”.

Asked whether Galliani was mounting a late comeback, Malagò added: “I’ve never been chasing in this game. It’s an electoral contest like many I’ve fought, even if there have been some strange positions.”.

Galliani, the former Milan and Monza executive, had his reply ready when he was approached leaving the PalaEur. He had been there for Italy’s basketball game against Turkey, which Malagò also attended.

“To my friend Giovanni, I’d say I stood because, as well as the technical components, a U-turn was also made by eight or nine Serie A clubs, including big ones like Juventus, Inter and Milan,” he mentioned with a smile.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of important saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

Recent findings suggest that “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

Industry observers note that “We have to change our mind promptly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

In a recent development, villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

It was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

In a recent development, mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY.

Nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had said before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations mentioned it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

When Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

According to recent reports, robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

Industry observers note that “We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa said. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

Sources indicate that “We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”.

Emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

According to recent reports, after a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery mentioned. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

Sources indicate that “It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa remarked. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that large regions of chromosomes are organized into a state known as heterochromatin. This densely packed form of DNA represses gene activity. Curiously, some families of clustered genes can be activated even though they are packed as heterochromatin. Writing in Nature, Buckley et al.1 report findings that explain this paradox: they show how opposing mechanisms that control the organization of heterochromatin promote the stochastic activation of genes in the protocadherin (Pcdh) gene cluster, thereby supporting proper nervous-system development.

Enzo Maresca has echoed Mauricio Pochettino’s punchy criticism of refereeing displays by claiming that some recent decisions against Manchester City are among the worst he has ever witnessed.

The absorbing rivalry between titans Erling Haaland and Gabriel – a battle renowned for excessive physicality - returns when City go to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.

And Maresca suggested that key calls in City’s recent winless run have contributed to them falling six points behind Mikel Arteta’s leaders.

Industry observers note that asked whether Haaland is treated unfairly by officials, the Italian remarked: ‘I can see that, to be honest. I can see also more things in the last four or five games - probably since the international break.

Sources indicate that ‘I’ve never seen in my life a player touch the ball with both arms and no penalty. For instance against Brighton, (Lewis) Dunk. I never seen it in my life. If you remember, both. No penalty. The other one was like volleyball.’.

Sources indicate that the second complaint from that Brighton defeat was an appeal for handball against Lukas Vuskovic, when Diego Gomez headed into the defender’s outstretched arm. The league’s Key Match Incidents panel voted 3-2 in favour of Craig Pawson’s decision not to award a penalty for Dunk’s handball.

Maresca suggested that key calls in City’s recent winless run have contributed to them falling six points behind Mikel Arteta’s leaders.

Newly introduced Manchester United boss Pochettino stated last weekend that with VAR, the league possesses ‘the best car but we need to drive it in the right way’ following Leny Yoro’s sending off at Liverpool.

Maresca’s analysis also partly centred on how VAR is being used as he raised Haaland’s disallowed goal against Fulham at the weekend, when the striker was adjudged to have fouled Bernd Leno and VAR stuck with the on-field decision.

‘The last game against Fulham, if you just stop (the image) when the goalkeeper has the ball there, it looks like (a foul), but the dynamic is he is not catching the ball,’ Maresca added.

It has been revealed that ‘Even the keeper does not believe that he was. Yes, there are fouls for Erling, but I can see also in the last games from the international break things that I don’t like, that for me are clear. But the referee is there, they decide, so we need to adapt.’.

Haaland has talked up his enthusiasm for going up against Gabriel this week and should be reinvigorated for the challenge after cutting a forlorn figure during and after the 2-2 draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The 26-year-old appeared downbeat during media interviews immediately after the game, sparking a discussion over his current frame of mind.

Maresca insisted that the striker’s mood is in line with other players as they strive to break free of a disappointing set of performances.

Industry observers note that ‘Erling is a winner,’ the City manager said. ‘It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games but it’s not just Erling, it's everyone. Don't forget that two weeks ago or three weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch (after beating Brighton in the Carabao Cup).

In a recent development, asked whether Haaland is treated unfairly by officials, the Italian noted: ‘I can see that, to be honest. I can see also more things in the last four or five games'.

‘You can write or think many different things, but the reality is sometimes much easier: Erling is upset, like I'm upset because we're not winning games. And when we were winning games everyone was happy. But this is our job, this is football, that's why we need to maintain the balance.’.

Haaland has admitted that he needs to improve in front of goal after scoring just once in his last five club games, yet Maresca believes the problems instead lie in quality consistent service.

‘I think he is gesticulating in the same way when we were winning games and he was not receiving balls,’ he stated. ‘Erling is a No 9, the No 9’s live day by day for goals.

Recent findings suggest that ‘When we drop the opposition inside the box and he is inside the box, he is the king there. The problem is that most of the teams now, because they are so aggressive, they come higher on the pitch, so you need him also to link a little bit. We need him in different ways.

It has been revealed that ‘I'm not a magician, there is a transition here. It's normal. We have eight, nine latest players, manager is new - you need time. You see at different clubs when they had transitions, how complicated it is.’.

#164486. Tech Report: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure

Tech Report: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.
  • For Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic.
  • Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.

For Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic. That relationship looks more complicated from Beijing and Moscow.

Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran. But both have broader interests in their relationships with the United States and may see Iran partly through the prism of their own negotiations with Washington.

That raises a central question: Can Trump's strategy of economically isolating Iran succeed if China and Russia refuse to fully cooperate?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

China is right now the most key destination for Iranian oil.

In 2025, it was reported that Chinese buyers took more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports, much of it through independent refiners and at a steep discount because of sanctions.

As China provided Tehran an economic lifeline, Iran also became increasingly dependent on Chinese manufactured goods, machinery and industrial inputs.

Mohsen Solhdoost, an assistant professor of international relations at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, indicates China is important to Washington's strategy but not decisive on its own.

"If the objective is to reduce Iranian export earnings, restrict access to equipment and make economic and military recovery more difficult, the United States can achieve substantial results without Chinese cooperation," he told DW.

But forcing Iran to accept Washington's preferred nuclear or regional policies is another matter.

"The ability to interrupt trade is much easier to demonstrate than the ability to determine another government's political choices," Solhdoost said.

That distinction has become more important as US sanctions enforcement and maritime blockade efforts have increased pressure on Iranian crude oil exports.

In November, Washington confirmed Task Force Iron Gate, an initiative aimed at disrupting the movement of sanctioned goods, military equipment and revenue through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Industry observers note that even so, these trade links have not disappeared. The commercial and security interests of countries including Iraq, Pakistan and Turkey mean that goods continue to move across the region, albeit under greater scrutiny.

As a result, China's role in Iran's economy remains significant, but Solhdoost argues that demand alone cannot sustain Iranian exports. The oil must be able to reach international markets.

"A Chinese buyer cannot keep Iranian export revenues flowing simply by remaining willing to buy if newly loaded tankers cannot reach the market," Solhdoost remarked.

This economic pressure is shaping Tehran's financial planning. A senior official at Iran's Initiative and Budget Organization recently said the government was preparing its 2027-2028 budget under several scenarios, including one in which oil revenue falls to zero.

That does not mean Iran has adopted a zero-oil budget, but considering such a scenario illustrates how seriously Tehran views the situation. At the same time, Chinese trade can preserve critical parts of the Iranian economy even if overall commerce shrinks.

Machinery, electronics, spare parts and industrial components can still reach Iran by rail and road. Such trade cannot replace maritime commerce at comparable scale or cost, but it can keep selected factories and infrastructure operating.

Such Chinese support could help Iran endure pressure without preventing economic deterioration, notes Solhdoost.

But even for Beijing, supporting Iran economically does not mean supporting every Iranian policy.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has maintained support for cooperation with Tehran while calling for negotiations, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and stable energy supplies.

Recent findings suggest that A prolonged conflict around Hormuz threatens wider energy supplies and global shipping. China therefore benefits from continued access to Iranian oil but also from regional stability.

Russia creates another obstacle to Iran's isolation. The two countries share access to the Caspian Sea and have expanded military, transport and economic cooperation.

Iranian officials have discussed ways of using Russian and northern trade routes to reduce the impact of American restrictions. There has also been speculation about oil swaps and deeper Russian assistance, although these claims remain difficult to verify.

Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, believes the summit should be viewed within a larger attempt to manage the wars in both Ukraine and the Middle East.

"Russia, China and the United States appear to be seeking constructive dialogue and results that could shape a new security architecture in the international system," Vakhshiteh told DW.

Solhdoost also warns against overstating Russian support for Iran.

The strategic partnership between Moscow and Tehran provides for security cooperation and efforts to counter unilateral sanctions, but it does not require Russia to enter a war on Iran's behalf.

Since Russia is deeply engaged in Ukraine, it likely has its own priorities in negotiations with Washington, says Solhdoost.

"Russia would prioritize its own national interests in negotiations with the US over Ukraine and Iran," he remarked.

Moscow could support Iran while simultaneously using its relationship with Tehran as leverage in talks with Trump over Ukraine.

For Iran, ties with China and Russia remain essential. They provide alternative trade routes, export markets and diplomatic support that complicate Washington's efforts to isolate Tehran.

Sources indicate that yet neither Beijing nor Moscow views Iran solely through the lens of strategic partnership. Both weigh support for Tehran against their own economic interests, security concerns and dealings with Washington.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

Industry observers note that A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

In a recent development, few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta noted, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

“There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

The result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

Referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

Industry observers note that it might be argued that Timber did not pull hard enough to prevent Isak from reaching the ball. But the defender grabbed the shirt and continued to hold it for a long time. It had to be a penalty. Little wonder Iraola mentioned Isak should dive next time. Who can blame him?

Industry observers note that what is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Arteta, not here to win friends – just to win matches and trophies.

“That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I have never seen before,” Declan Rice, who was also a stand-out performer and delivered a fine assist for the winner, said.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

In a recent development, “That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

It has been revealed that even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s back line. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

In a recent development, arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

In a recent development, in fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

In a recent development, and the only goal? Again, more frustration for Liverpool. It was well-constructed from Arsenal, but only after Alisson Becker’s loose goal kick, aimed towards Jérémy Jacquet, who was slow to react, was intercepted by Odegaard with Bruno Guimarães poking the ball to the right, where it was collected by Madueke.

There was an overlap by Rice and his low centre was precise and dangerous across the face of the six-yard area, with Virgil van Dijk unsure what to do. It ran beyond the far post where Kai Havertz side-footed home.

This Christmas, Everton in the Community is calling on supporters to help tackle loneliness and bring the true Christmas Spirit of the Blues to those who need it most.

Loneliness can affect anyone, at any time of the year. It could be an older person facing another Christmas without their loved ones, a young person struggling to find where they belong, a parent finding it difficult to cope or someone surrounded by people but still feeling alone.

That's why the official charitable arm of Everton Football Club is launching Christmas Spirit of the Blues, a campaign dedicated to raising awareness of loneliness in all its forms and ensuring everyone knows there is somewhere they can turn.

Dedicated to breaking down barriers and supporting its local community since 1988, Everton in the Community delivers more than 50 inclusive, free programmes, each designed to tackle different societal challenges.

From supporting young people back into education and giving upcoming fathers access to vital support networks, to helping military veterans navigate life after the forces, each programme shares the same ambition - to improve confidence, provide a sense of belonging and remind people just how vital they are.

To launch the campaign, Everton in the Community brought together participants, staff, supporters and players past and present at Hill Dickinson Stadium for a special performance of the iconic Liverpool Express hit, Spirit of the Blues.

Liverpool-based brass band Allerton Brass performed a slowed-down version of the track, creating a poignant moment of togetherness and highlighting the power of music to bring people together.

Throughout the build-up to Christmas, the campaign will shine a light on the experiences of people who have faced loneliness and explore how finding support, friendship and a sense of belonging has made a difference to their lives.

Among those sharing their stories is Gina, who has found cherished friendships through Everton in the Community's Stand Together programme following the loss of her husband, and a young man whose experience of loneliness brought him to the brink of suicide.

The campaign will also hear from father-of-two Sean, who reached out to Everton in the Community in the middle of the night after his wife tragically died just 12 hours after giving birth to their second son.

“My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably.

“It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn't expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.”.

At a time when his world had been turned upside down, Sean says reaching out gave him someone to turn to when he felt he had nowhere else to go, and marked the first step towards navigating life without his wife.

Dan Halliday, Head of Fundraising at Everton in the Community, said: “For thousands of people across the Liverpool City Region and beyond, loneliness, social isolation and grief can feel even heavier at Christmas.

“The pressure to feel happy or the absence of familiar handwriting on a Christmas card can be painful reminders of what's missing.

In a recent development, “This Christmas, a donation to Everton in the Community could help someone feel seen, supported and part of something bigger. Together, we can make sure nobody has to face loneliness alone.”.

To donate to Everton in the Community and join our mission to end loneliness together, visit (insert link).

For more information about accessing support, visit https://www.evertoninthecommunity.org/projects/minds/accessing-mental-health-support/.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Thursday's meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" in Berlin sent a strong signal to Moscow that it was time to take negotiations to end the war in Ukraine seriously.

Sources indicate that speaking to DW during a visit to the South Caucasus, Wadephul described the summit as the largest meeting of Ukraine's supporters so far. The meeting represents the 18th set of high-level talks among the coalition's members.

He stated it demonstrated that allies remained firmly behind Kyiv in the fifth year of Russia's war and were ready to do "what was necessary to ensure Ukraine could negotiate from a position of strength.".

"The summit itself is already a success," he told DW.

It has been revealed that wadephul also welcomed the US initiative to restart peace negotiations. After nine months without progress, an initial meeting had taken place in Abu Dhabi, with a follow-up round planned and European participation expected.

"We are also preparing for the possibility that the negotiations will not be successful and that, over the coming winter, we will have to continue supplying Ukraine with heating, electricity and all essential supplies, including water," he said.

"And we will continue to stand by Ukraine militarily.".

He stressed that any peace agreement must include security guarantees to protect Ukraine against future Russian attacks.

In earlier comments during his trip to the South Caucasus, Wadephul said that Ukraine and Europe must be involved in any negotiations over the future of Ukraine.

Wadephul did, however, welcome the trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

"Every conversation that takes place is a good conversation," he told DW during a visit to Azerbaijan on Wednesday.

Later on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin mentioned he had invited Europeans to Moscow for talks on the potential structure of future talks to end the war.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vasilije Adžić has undergone knee surgery, and the Juventus loanee could miss the rest of the season with Sassuolo.

According to a statement from Juventus, the 20-year-old Montenegro international suffered a sprain and bruising to his right knee in Montenegro’s Nations League game against Cyprus on 15 November. Tests revealed “a small osteochondral detachment”, meaning a piece of bone and cartilage had come away inside the joint.

It has been revealed that adžić had surgery on Thursday at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon, where Juventus captain Manuel Locatelli was also operated on in September. He has now started the rehabilitation programme “aimed at returning to competitive activity”.

Recent findings suggest that neither Juventus nor Sassuolo have given a timeframe for his recovery. However, TuttoMercatoWeb suggests the need for surgery points to a lengthy absence, with a real risk he won’t play again before the end of the 2026-27 season.

It’s a cruel blow for a player who started his loan in style. Adžić scored in three consecutive Serie A games in September, including a curling winner off the bench in Sassuolo’s 3-2 victory over Juventus. His form has tailed off since then, and he has three goals and one assist in nine league appearances.

The injury could also affect his future. Sassuolo paid €500,000 to take him on loan in the summer and included an option to buy fixed at €12m, while Juventus kept a buy-back clause. A long spell out leaves both clubs with little to go on when they decide his future next summer.

The Brazilian’s situation has become increasingly complicated following Scott Parker’s appointment earlier this month.

The newly introduced manager has not included Pablo in any of his four matchday squads since taking charge, raising further doubts about his prospects of securing regular first-team football.

He has also struggled to make an impression in the Championship, scoring just once in nine league appearances this season.

West Ham could therefore consider arranging a loan move rather than accepting such a disappointing permanent transfer fee.

A successful spell elsewhere, potentially in Portugal, could help the striker rebuild his confidence and restore some of his market value.

For now, the Hammers must decide how best to limit their losses.

Newcastle fans turn on Jaissle as defeat triggers relegation concerns

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5161 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.
  • Industry observers note that this was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce.
  • The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

Industry observers note that this was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

In a recent development, this was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

“I have to take the responsibility,” he stated. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the blueprint. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

“As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the blueprint disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it shows.”.

Newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

Sources indicate that if they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Recent findings suggest that concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight new signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

According to recent reports, A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat promptly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

There was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

Everton, just as they had in their Carabao Cup win last week, looked comfortable. Recognising how easy it was to nullify Newcastle’s game strategy, they offered an attacking threat of their own.

A rising shot from Merlin Röhl briefly had goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek worried. A free-kick into the Newcastle box caused panic. James Tarkowski won the first header, but Thierno Barry swung and missed with his left foot.

Recent findings suggest that the groans began to turn into boos and whistles. Jaissle’s side could barely string more than two passes together. It felt precarious.

Sources indicate that this is not an easy place to play football when the crowd airs its displeasure. As the first half limped on, there were players in black and white who looked like they could not handle the pressure.

It was a horrible game of football. With the last kick of the half, Everton should have taken the lead, Harrison Armstrong picked out Barry inside the box, but he made a mess of the finish. The referee’s whistle was accompanied by boos and a scream of “sort it out” from behind Jaissle’s technical area.

Sources indicate that he did not follow those blunt instructions. Everton took the lead in such simple fashion and all Jaissle and his coaching staff could do was shake their heads at each other. Tyrique George was played in far too easily from a free-kick but his shot should have been saved by Hornicek. It was straight at the Czech, but it went through him and it left Barry with a tap in. Newcastle appealed for both a foul on Fabian Schar and an offside but got neither.

According to recent reports, thierno Barry puts Everton ahead after Tyrique George's shot isn't dealt with by Lukáš Horníček! 🔵 https://t.co/oRXsrwbOhz.

In a recent development, everton had the lead and it was so easy and straightforward. They waited for Newcastle to give the ball away and then broke at speed. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was superb and forced a fingertip save from Hornicek. From the resulting corner, Hornicek was needed again to keep out Jake O’Brien’s header.

Newcastle tried to gain some momentum and finally created a chance. Harvey Barnes curled a cross to the far post. It bounced awkwardly but Anthony Elanga somehow failed to bundle it across the line.

Getting the first goal was notable. Incredibly proud of the team all the time because their effort is unquestionable. There is not a lot of them but they are doing a great job and hope it continues.

“We are creating chances, that is the massive thing for me. Thierno [Barry] has had some big opportunities. He was on the spot today. I was worried ‘was he on or offside at the time?’. I do not think anyone enjoys playing the same team twice so quickly. So for us to win both is hugely important for us. We want to get back to the top end of the league, it is incredibly tight.”.

“I think it was probably our best performance of the season, I thought we were terrific in the first half and could have scored two or three. Thierno [Barry] gets the goal again for us. There is a lot on his shoulders, he is our only recognised striker so hopefully he can keep putting the ball in the net like he has done. He is harsh on himself but his numbers are through the roof in terms of running. A clean sheet is massive for us. It is a long old season. We take it game by game but tonight feels good and we can look forward to Friday [against Coventry].”.

Sources indicate that hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a upcoming guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport. Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters. Disabled sports broadcaster Andy Stevenson hosted the event, with executives from both Level Playing Field and the Equality and Human Rights Commission addressing attendees. Panel discussions also allowed for insight from industry experts and disabled supporters to be shared with officials from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport, the Sports Grounds Safety Authority and governing bodies across a range of sports. Everton officials and members of Everton Disabled Supporters' Association (EDSA) were among representatives of disabled supporter groups, clubs and venues from across the country. "Accessibility and inclusivity were key factors in the design of Hill Dickinson Stadium and, since its opening, we have continued to learn from feedback and refine our offering to create the best possible experience for all our supporters and visitors. "Hosting an event like today's allows us to share work we are incredibly proud of, but also to strengthen our relationships with key stakeholders, with supporter groups and to continue that learning journey."Chair of Level Playing Field, Tony Taylor, said: “Today marks an important milestone, as we strive to make attending live sport genuinely accessible for all disabled fans. “It has been our pleasure to lead on this project and channel the input from different stakeholders to define a set of standards and outline a roadmap to deliver access and inclusion. “Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition has the potential to make a dramatic difference to the experiences of so many disabled supporters, and it is important that we all come together to realise this opportunity.” Hill Dickinson Stadium, officially opened in August 2025, offers more wheelchair bays than any other English club stadium and accessible viewing platforms located on multiples levels. The stadium is also equipped with a state-of-the-art sensory room, quiet rooms, Changing Places facilities and low-level counters, as well as providing step-free access to all concourse levels. In addition to hosting Premier League matches, the stadium has become an established home for international football, rugby league and rugby union. To learn more about accessibility provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, click here. Further details about the Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and how to access the guide, can be found at levelplayingfield.org.uk.

Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a new guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport.

Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters.

Disabled sports broadcaster Andy Stevenson hosted the event, with executives from both Level Playing Field and the Equality and Human Rights Commission addressing attendees.

Panel discussions also allowed for insight from industry experts and disabled supporters to be shared with officials from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport, the Sports Grounds Safety Authority and governing bodies across a range of sports.

Everton officials and members of Everton Disabled Supporters' Association (EDSA) were among representatives of disabled supporter groups, clubs and venues from across the country.

Christopher Massam, Accessibility Lead at Everton Football Club, said: "We are truly honoured to host the launch of Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and to bring together so many great minds and voices on what is a vitally important subject.

"As a Club, we have worked closely with Level Playing Field and EDSA for a number of years as part of our efforts to continually appraise and enhance the accessibility provision across all our stadiums and sites.

"Accessibility and inclusivity were key factors in the design of Hill Dickinson Stadium and, since its opening, we have continued to learn from feedback and refine our offering to create the best possible experience for all our supporters and visitors.

"Hosting an event like today's allows us to share work we are incredibly proud of, but also to strengthen our relationships with key stakeholders, with supporter groups and to continue that learning journey.".

Chair of Level Playing Field, Tony Taylor, stated: “Today marks an crucial milestone, as we strive to make attending live sport genuinely accessible for all disabled fans.

“It has been our pleasure to lead on this project and channel the input from different stakeholders to define a set of standards and outline a roadmap to deliver access and inclusion.

“Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition has the potential to make a dramatic difference to the experiences of so many disabled supporters, and it is key that we all come together to realise this opportunity.”.

Hill Dickinson Stadium, officially opened in August 2025, offers more wheelchair bays than any other English club stadium and accessible viewing platforms located on multiples levels.

The stadium is also equipped with a state-of-the-art sensory room, quiet rooms, Changing Places facilities and low-level counters, as well as providing step-free access to all concourse levels.

In addition to hosting Premier League matches, the stadium has become an established home for international football, rugby league and rugby union.

To learn more about accessibility provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, click here.

Further details about the Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and how to access the guide, can be found at levelplayingfield.org.uk.

From young players to women's game to the national team, how can SFA duo Maxwell and Mulholland possibly be trusted to move things forward?
