📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:33 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • With the Scottish FA’s widely trumpeted proposal to get young players more game time now lying in a ditch off the M74, it was hard not to raise a wry smile at the midweek communique from Hampden over the intention to come up with some other kind of just-as-good idea somewhere in the new year.
  • ‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right,’ it closed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:33 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EST, 27 November 2026.

With the Scottish FA’s widely trumpeted proposal to get young players more game time now lying in a ditch off the M74, it was hard not to raise a wry smile at the midweek communique from Hampden over the intention to come up with some other kind of just-as-good idea somewhere in the new year.

‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right,’ it closed.

According to recent reports, bit late for that chat, is it not? Shouldn’t that work behind the scenes have been done before the grand summit at St Andrews back at the start of September when SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell and his chief football officer Craig Mulholland revealed themselves lords and saviours of the national game with their scheme to shoehorn Under-21 players – no matter how good, bad or indifferent they may be – into club sides all over the country?

It all sounded good at the time, of course, if you put your head in the clouds and daydreamed over how pretty the world might be if everyone just got along.

Handwringers nationwide fell over themselves to simper the usual platitudes over how self-interest must be sacrificed for the greater good. There was probably some kind of online petition to link hands between all 42 senior grounds for a chorus of Kumbaya.

Meanwhile, anyone who has the faintest idea of the realpolitik of Scottish football looked at what was on the table and knew it was destined for the knacker’s yard.

SFA top brass Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell flank Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

The SFA should have been consulting their more prominent clubs before going public over what might work and what might not, moulding something that the teams which matter were willing to support.

Instead, almost half the outfits in the Premiership blew their proposals out of the water in the end.

The sound of silence from Hampden, of course, had already become deafening as they realised they’d made a pig’s ear of it. Right now, it looks like everyone is back to the drawing board.

It has been revealed that it’s embarrassing for the SFA. It has just made Maxwell and Mulholland look like they are incapable of taking the game with them on vital matters.

In a recent development, naturally, though, there wasn’t a single word from Haudit or Daudit in that press release to more or less confirm a major reverse ferret is going to be required. When things go belly-up, the high heid yins at Hampden are often nowhere to be seen.

Maxwell was too busy turning his mind to other matters during the week anyway, namely the fact that Scotland will be co-hosting the Women’s World Cup with the rest of the UK in 2035.

Given that was the only actual bid, the award of the event was hardly earth-shattering, but that didn’t stop Maxwell treating it as his Next Massive Thing.

Maxwell has been in position at the SFA for more than eight years but has lacked real impact.

It has been revealed that ‘I think it is going to be an absolutely transformational event to host in the UK and Ireland,’ he gushed. ‘The hard work starts now in terms of legacy and impact and driving everything we can from it.’.

Hmmmm. Nice as it is that he’s managed to put being custard-pied at home by a large chunk of the Premiership over youth opportunities behind him, it might be wise to take Maxwell’s words over the women’s game with a pinch of salt.

He also called Scotland going to their first World Cup in 2019 ‘transformational’. Months later, Glasgow City won their 13th straight title with a ten-goal win over Motherwell on a council-run pitch in Wishaw in front of 100 people with no shelter, no seating and no obvious way for an ambulance to gain entry should a medical emergency occur. One Motherwell player had to nick across to the attached sports centre to get a chair for an injured team-mate to sit on.

A year had passed since the national team’s qualification, but there was still no kind of plan for the £400,000 prize money that they earned.

Recent findings suggest that city’s Hayley Lauder, who’d been at the World Cup in France, tweeted: ‘Just won a league title in a public park at a sports centre. Not how I envisaged the game in 2019.’.

It was a message that encapsulated the catastrophic failure to build on the incredible platform France 2019 provided under Maxwell’s reign.

Scotland celebrate an Erin Cuthbert goal against Argentina in 2019 before it all turned sour.

That should have been the real launchpad for the women’s game here. Instead, it turned into a toxic shambles that killed any kind of momentum.

Industry observers note that progress since has been nothing like what it should have been. The national team, out to reach the next World Cup in next week’s play-off against Sweden, has been mired in failure. The women’s game lives back in the shadows amid pitiful attendances and an inability – or, it sometimes seems, refusal – to sell itself.

According to recent reports, yet, it could all have been so different. Just remember the scene back in ‘19. Scotland have to beat Argentina to make the last 16. A TV audience of six million watched the meeting with England earlier in the campaign.

The drama as Shelley Kerr’s side let slip a three-goal lead with 16 minutes to play – eventually drawing 3-3 thanks to a stoppage-time penalty retaken after an initial save by keeper Lee Gibson – was just incredible. It was the talk of the nation the next day.

And, then, it all just died a death. The head coach Shelley Kerr eventually coughed to the fact ‘a few drinks’ had been taken before a debrief the next day that reportedly left some players in tears.

No one wanted to talk about it. No one ever has, really. Yours truly asked Glasgow City for an interview with Gibson, then Alexander, in the early stages of the following season.

Top-flight matches between teams in the SWPL regularly take place on glorified public pitches.

According to recent reports, she’d been at the centre of a major global event. There was a story to be told. City insisted all requests had to be run past the SFA and their media office pretty much made it clear it wouldn’t be happening before she had even been asked.

In a recent development, no one told their stories of the biggest event in the history of women’s football here. Not properly. It felt like some kind of Omerta had been put in place over it.

Industry observers note that kerr, inexplicably, was allowed to keep her job by Maxwell and then failed to make it to Euro 2022. Instead, that year was marked by the women’s team, with Kerr gone, threatening to take legal action against the SFA over a lack of resources – with then captain Rachel Corsie referring to ‘years of iniquity, disrespect, and, in some cases, abuse.’.

Yeah, the aftermath of France 2019 was ‘transformational’ all right. It transformed the hundreds of thousands of folk compelled to watch women’s football on national TV that summer back into people who forget it even exists.

Colleagues tell me there was no scope midweek to even interview anyone in a position of power within the SFA over what should have been a Good News Story regarding 2035. Hardly ‘driving everything we can from it’, is it?

I mean, how can you trust the likes of Maxwell to harness the opportunities afforded by that event – or Euro 2028 on home soil – when reflecting upon the raging binfire France 2019 became?

Mulholland is a regular sight being entertained by football matches up and down the country.

How can you trust him and Mulholland to get it right on forging pathways for young players when they made such a Horlicks of trying to implement that poorly-planned proposal for Scotland-eligible Under-21s and failed again when changing it to involve Under-23s?

There’s a far wider issue with the production of players that involves going deep into the SFA’s own workings, addressing that lack of knowledge St Mirren boss Craig McLeish talked about at the lower levels of grassroots.

Indeed, there are problems all over the SFA. With refereeing standards. With VAR. With Steve Clarke admitting he forced the top brass into ‘panicking’ before the World Cup and giving him a new four-year deal.

If Maxwell and Mulholland’s blue-eyed boy Sebastien Pocognoli doesn’t start looking like he’s got a handle on his role as Clarke’s successor as national boss after a grim start to his reign, everything points to the two of them having to go the same way as their original Youth Strategy. By being binned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have triggered a one-year extension on Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ending Milan’s hopes of signing him on a free transfer next summer.

According to The Athletic, the club captain is now tied to Old Trafford until June 2028. Fernandes had been entering the final year of his deal and recently confirmed that talks over a fresh contract had been put on hold, with both sides wanting to focus on improving results.

By exercising the option, United have stopped the 32-year-old from negotiating with foreign clubs from 1 January, when he would otherwise have been free to agree a pre-contract.

According to recent reports, that doesn’t rule out a move next year, but any club wanting Fernandes will now have to pay a fee. Milan are among the European clubs monitoring him, along with interest from Saudi Arabia, and United have already identified possible replacements.

The Portuguese midfielder’s future had looked uncertain after Michael Carrick dropped him for a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth. That followed his public criticism of the team’s tactics after a 4-1 Champions League loss to Como.

Since then, however, Fernandes has kept the captaincy under latest coach Mauricio Pochettino and scored twice in Wednesday’s 2-2 draw at Sporting CP.

China’s AI-powered smart-city model is going global

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (966 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • To understand the Chinese smart city, it helps to know that twenty-first-century infrastructure, technology and policy increasingly makes the whole of China a single, interconnected economic unit.
  • So, if the goal of a ‘smart city’ is to use substantial data and AI to outsource governance functions, keeping everything running smoothly, then maybe we should think of China as a single city, with its different provinces and megalopolises as neighbourhoods with their own special roles.
  • China’s 15th five-year strategy unveiled earlier this year sees the country in this way, too, by entrusting certain functions to different cities and regions, and with rural areas also playing an essential role.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To understand the Chinese smart city, it helps to know that twenty-first-century infrastructure, technology and policy increasingly makes the whole of China a single, interconnected economic unit. Trains, planes and autonomous vehicles shuttle about, with the centre of megacities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen merely being in the middle of ‘one-hour circles’ for commuters that allow them to reach anywhere in the wider urban area with ease. Previous barriers to the internal movement of workers, such the hukou system, which restricted access to public services based on a person’s birthplace, are being removed, making it easier for people to compete for jobs across the country. And all the while, the Internet supercharges these shifts to a nationwide marketplace, backed by an ever-expanding supply of data centres. Sichuanese farmers of organic lemons now livestream from rural villages on apps such as Xiaohongshu or Douyin as they compete for city restaurateurs to buy their products.

So, if the goal of a ‘smart city’ is to use substantial data and AI to outsource governance functions, keeping everything running smoothly, then maybe we should think of China as a single city, with its different provinces and megalopolises as neighbourhoods with their own special roles. For instance, three of China’s megacities each have their own crucial function: Beijing regulates and invests in fundamental research; Shanghai is home to multinational corporations, frontier research in AI and biotech, and finance; and the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen and Guangzhou, is home to innovative manufacturers, such as electric vehicle producer BYD, tech giant Huawei and consumer electronics firm DJI.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

China’s 15th five-year strategy unveiled earlier this year sees the country in this way, too, by entrusting certain functions to different cities and regions, and with rural areas also playing an essential role. In the northeast, farming is increasingly carried out with the use of drones and significant data by state-owned companies such as Beidahuang. In Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang, data centres are powered by abundant solar and wind energy, where they calculate how the self-driving cars of China’s eastern seaboard should navigate roads or process the AI that helps to keep the country’s state-of-the-art high-speed train network running on time.

This approach on data is embodied by 东数西算 (roughly translated as ‘east data, west compute’), a national-level strategic project to channel data from developed eastern regions to resource-rich western regions for processing and storage using eight data-centre ‘hubs’ located across the country. Eastern megacities generate the vast majority of China’s data and AI requests, but they bring skyrocketing land costs, power shortages and cooling difficulties that make hosting data centres unattractive. Instead, the solar farms of Xinjiang’s deserts and the wind farms of the Mongolian steppe are used to provide renewable, cheap energy to data centres.

Sources indicate that one key example is Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia, which has been transformed from a traditional farming region into a prominent data powerhouse, earning the name ‘Grassland Cloud Valley’. The energy costs in Ulanqab are low, because the government has been installing massive renewable capacity, relying on the area’s abundant wind and solar resources. Mongolia is cold for most of the year, so data centres use standard air cooling rather than massive air-conditioning set-ups — effectively, they just cover the servers with plastic and leave the door open for wintry winds to circulate. Major firms such as Huawei, Alibaba, Kuaishou and Apple have constructed large-scale cloud bases in Ulanqab. The region houses China’s largest intelligent computing centre for autonomous driving (Fuyao), built by Xpeng Motors and Alibaba Cloud, which has helped make it 170 times faster to train self-driving models. It means an autonomous taxi driving around Beijing is effectively being controlled by servers in the far-away desert of Inner Mongolia.

Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.

The case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement. Zverev, who won the French and US Open in 2026, is alleged to have told French publication L'Equipe that: "I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.".

As Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued... without any finding of guilt, and the presumption of innocence remains unaffected.".

However, Zverev's statement has harmed Patea's standing and her career as an influencer, according to her lawyer, Michael Scheele.

It has been revealed that "What she suffered after this interview in L'Equipe was published is nothing but a shitstorm. It's also detrimental to her business," Scheele told DW.

"We still don't know the truth objectively and we have an agreement in which he committed not to talk about the incident and the case at all," he added.

In a recent development, however, in the statement sent to DW, Zverev's lawyers asserted that "there has been no breach of any contractual obligations or violation of Ms. Patea’s personality rights.".

Sources indicate that zverev had made similar comments before. On the day the settlement was reached, the tennis pro spoke to reporters at the 2024 French Open.

According to recent reports, "That's what dropping the case is: That is innocence. They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day," he said.

The lawsuit, seen by DW, states that Zverev should be subject to "a fine of up to €250,000 ($275,000) to be determined for each instance of violation — and, in the event that such fine cannot be collected, substitute custodial detention of up to six months," should he be found guilty.

Zverev's lawyers reject the allegations.

In a recent development, "Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit. If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion protected by Article 5(1) of the German Basic Law," they said.

According to recent reports, "Our client would merely have expressed his personal conviction that he had done everything in his power to refute the allegations made against him and that he considers his innocence to have been confirmed by the outcome of the criminal proceedings. "He is fully entitled to hold and express this view.".

The law firm, Schertz Bergmann, added that: "Unlike the opposing counsel, we intend to conduct these proceedings in court rather than in the press.".

Scheele stated he and his client did not want to go back to court but were frustrated in their efforts to resolve matters in other ways.

"We went forward writing to him in a polite way, asking him to sign and to declare that he's not going to repeat what he stated. And he didn't reply. So we wrote twice more, no reply.

Recent findings suggest that "That's when we had to decide to go to court, which was not the aim at the beginning. We wanted to avoid it, but we had no other choice.".

Zverev, now resident in Monaco, is right now playing in the season-ending ATP Finals tournament in Turin.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that manchester United are in dire need of a newly introduced left-back in January.
  • In a recent development, luke Shaw is nearing a return to full fitness, however, and is expected to take back that spot soon, after missing the last seven weeks with a muscle problem.
  • According to recent reports, according to Sport Witness, United are showing interest in Sporting left-back Maxi Araujo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that manchester United are in dire need of a newly introduced left-back in January. Lisandro Martinez was used in that position for the 2-2 draw at Sporting CP on Wednesday, after Diogo Dalot was dropped following another dismal performance in the 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool.

In a recent development, luke Shaw is nearing a return to full fitness, however, and is expected to take back that spot soon, after missing the last seven weeks with a muscle problem. Despite that, Shaw has struggled even when available and United should look to upgrade in the transfer window.

According to recent reports, according to Sport Witness, United are showing interest in Sporting left-back Maxi Araujo. It's understood the Reds have been monitoring the Uruguay international for a number of months now, and, of course, saw him up close at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that araujo has a £67million release clause in his contract, but United could get him for less in January. As well as that, he is believed to be 'very open' about making the move to Old Trafford and has previously expressed his desire to play in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that it could be a smart signing, but United should avoid Araujo and instead target someone else. While the 26-year-old did win Sporting's second spot-kick as he was fouled by Senne Lammens and was an attacking threat, he has some big flaws to his game.

Indeed, in the draw against United, Araujo lost possession NINE times, completing just 86 per cent of his passes (38/46) and having one out of four successful dribbles. He didn't make a single accurate pass into the box and completed just one successful cross.

In a recent development, alongside that, Araujo's defending flattered to deceive. He won just 42 per cent (8/19) of his duels, one tackle and committed three fouls. The ex-Puebla and Toluca man started as a left wing-back and often got caught out with Amad Diallo having joy on that side.

While he can be strong going forward, Araujo does struggle defensively and has proven that on a number of occasions this season. None more so than in the 3-2 defeat to LASK in the Champions League last month, where he could have done better for all three goals. He didn't stop the cross for LASK's first, while both the second and third came down his side.

Considering that and the fact United have conceded the most goals (36) in Europe's top five leagues across all competitions this season, the Reds need a more defensive-minded left-back and Newcastle United's Lewis Hall would be perfect.

It has been revealed that the Athletic have reported that United remain interested in Hall, and although it could be difficult for them to persuade Newcastle to sell in January, the Reds need to do all they can to sign him. The England international is one of the best left-sided defenders in the Premier League right now and would be an exceptional addition, even if he is expensive.

Industry observers note that defensively, there are not too many better than Hall about. He produced an impressive performance to keep Lamine Yamal quiet in England's famous 3-2 win against Spain earlier this month, and has been a nemesis for many a right-winger in recent times.

He can attack as well. Indeed, in 113 appearances for Newcastle, Hall has directly contributed to 13 goals. Earlier this season, Hall found the net in a 2-1 win at Hull City and grabbed an assist in a 2-2 draw at home against Bournemouth.

Sources indicate that united should go all out to bring Hall to Old Trafford. He should be their first-choice target with Araujo and Antonee Robinson behind. Despite their league position, the Reds should be targeting the best in class - and Hall is just that.

According to recent reports, former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe heaped praise on the "outstanding" Hall last season, despite leaving him out of the starting line-up to face Arsenal. “Lewis is an outstanding player and you never for any second doubt his qualities and what he can bring to the team," Howe said, when asked the reason behind Dan Burn's inclusion in the team at left-back.

Meanwhile, Pochettino worked with Hall for a brief period at Chelsea and wished him well as he moved to Newcastle. Acknowledging his potential, the Argentine said: “He was unlucky that he could not play [more], but he has a good future and I hope he can settle well there.”.

Thomas Tuchel hailed Hall's progress during the recent international break, saying he made a "massive impression" on the England team.

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

Industry observers note that roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

In a recent development, united fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

In a recent development, whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Recent findings suggest that carrick may at least have been encouraged by some of the things Bruno Fernandes said after the game, not least that he warranted being dropped against Bournemouth. And it was the captain who kick-started the fightback against Roma, albeit at the second attempt.

Industry observers note that he had won the penalty after being fouled by Gianluca Mancini only to then contrive to miss it. But a retake was ordered for encroachment and, given a second bite at the cherry, Fernandes made no mistake.

When Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury within seconds of the restart as he burst into the penalty area, Carrick must have wondered what else could go wrong.

But as United went hell for leather, the home supporters who had spent much of the first half attacking the owners and staging a number of colourful protest acts, suddenly found their voice in a very different way.

From being an atmosphere in which the players clearly felt cowed, Old Trafford was now rallying behind its men in red – and it helped to shake Roma in the process. They had been such good value for their lead, but now they were rocking, and United smelled blood.

There was wave after wave of attack as Roma desperately and often frantically tried to defend their goal, and it took a bad mistake from Leonardo Balerdi, who swung at thin air from Fernandes’s cross and missed the ball, to hand Cunha the chance to equalise.

On the pitch, United were all over the place. Had he done, he would have seen Matías Soulé unmarked and in acres of space with Diogo Dalot, United’s left-back, caught high up the pitch. Soulé made no mistake with his finish.

In a recent development, at that point, no one could have reckoned on the comeback that followed. Where it leads, who knows.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

“It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” stated Carrick.

Industry observers note that “I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

Industry observers note that asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

Industry observers note that “Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys highlighted an awful lot,” he noted.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he revealed everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

“It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

In a recent development, “But today was important to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

“It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

It has been revealed that “It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans said: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, big character, big fight.”.

According to recent reports, “We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

According to recent reports, as for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we demonstrated what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

Galatasaray are already 2-0 up on Stuttgart, while Sporting have found the breakthrough against Shakhtar Donetsk in the early kick-offs.

Manchester United fans are planning a series of in-stadium demonstrations at Old Trafford tonight in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s ownership.

Thousands of green and gold balloons – a nod to the club’s original colours as Newton Heath – are set to be released from the Stretford End when the Champions League music plays out ahead of kick-off.

There had been plans to bring a banner into the stadium bearing the words: “No latest stadium, we want new owners” but that was blocked, apparently on the grounds of Uefa’s inability to sanction it in time.

The Glazers and Ratcliffe have come under growing attack this season with the club’s regular match going supporters at war with the owners.

A separate fans’ group has also been encouraging fans to join in anti Glazers and Ratcliffe chants in the 21st minute or, more specifically, after 20 minutes and 5 seconds: 20.05 is a nod to 2005, the year the Glazers completed their hostile takeover at Old Trafford.

The main surprise for Roma is in goal, as with first-choice keeper Svilar out already, it has been confirmed that backup keeper Pierluigi Gollini has injured his back today. He has been replaced by Colombian Devis Vásquez in goal.

Roma: Vásquez; Balerdi, Mancini, Hermoso; Rensch, de Roon, Mora, Wesley; Soulé, Cristante; Malen.

We have confirmation, Martínez is on the bench. He is replaced by Ayden Heaven while Bruno Fernandes is still with the captain’s armband in midfield. Kobbie Mainoo gets the nod as he returns from injury, along with Mateus Cunha and Mason Mount.

Your United team for tonight's #UCL clash 👊 https://t.co/TD9F6RjeAB.

Lisandro Martínez has been dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his red card madness against Chelsea.

The United manager has opted to pair Ayden Heaven in central defence with Harry Maguire for the Roma game with Martinez dropping to the bench.

The Argentina defender received a second yellow card for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea when he was also culpable for the first goal.

Martinez has been in dire form this season and was fined and publicly apologised after publicly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and the Old Trafford board in the wake of the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Kobbie Mainoo returns to midfield after missing the last four games through injury.

Ayden Heaven has just come out to speak with Prime Video, which has led Gabby Logan to assume that means that Lisandro Martínez will not start for Michael Carrick tonight.

Speaking with her, former United legend Wayne Rooney has mentioned the Argentine has “simply not been good enough” and should not necessarily feature again under Carrick.

When Alan Shearer was asked if he would include Martínez on a team sheet tonight, he did not mince his words, calling him a “liability”.

Ahead of the confirmed line-ups coming out shortly, there are certain players we know we will not be seeing today.

Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Benjamin Sesko (shin) remain sidelined for United, while Marcus Rashford and Amad Diallo will be assessed before the match.

There are no new concerns for Gasperini after his side’s latest match, the 5-2 win over Udinese, but he remains unable to select Muhammed Bah (ACL), Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone (thigh), Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) and first-choice keeper Mile Svilar (stress fracture, foot).

Happy Tuesday and thanks for tuning in to tonight’s coverage of Manchester United against Roma.

According to recent reports, it’s matchday four of the Champions League and Michael Carrick’s side host their Serie A opponents having failed to win any of their last nine matches across all competitions. Since their win against Sabah back in September (must feel like years ago to Carrick), they have suffered chastening defeats in Europe to Atlético Madrid and then Cesc Fabregas’s Como. This has been coupled with dismal performances in the Premier League, most recently a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea, where Lisandro Martínez was sent off for two ridiculous fouls.

Lisandro Martinez is shown a second yellow card following a VAR review 🟥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max ➡️https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/VLcAMNdqgZ.

All in all, there is the feeling that Carrick is simply a dead man walking, limping towards the international break after the United hierarchy decided on a stay of execution in their crisis talks earlier this month. If the beleaguered manager has any hope at all of hanging on to his job, he needs convincing results tonight and against Aston Villa on the weekend.

Despite the doom-mongering that circles the club, Carrick maintains that he has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes following his captain’s public criticisms of the club, insisting that “the dressing room is a good place” in his pre-match press conference (more on that to come).

In a recent development, the visitors on the other hand, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini – who replaced Claudio Ranieri last summer – are certainly having a better time of it. They got off to a slow start in Europe, drawing with Fernebahce in their opening match but coming agonisingly close to stunning Real Madrid on matchday two at home. They went 3-1 up before three late goals snatched victory for Madrid.

In a recent development, they bounced back with a convincing 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava and their domestic campaign is off to an incredibly promising start. They are presently unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and three draws. They sit third and are the highest scoring side, with 28 goals from their 10 games. Free-flowing though their attack is, there a certainly defensive frailties there to exploit as they conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, as well as two in both matches against Cagliari and Udinese.

According to recent reports, it has been 19 years since Carrick was part of a United side that thrashed Roma 7-1 at Old Trafford, with the midfielder scoring two. Tonight he faces that same opponent with his job hanging by a thread and it remains to be seen if his team can produce any semblance of that spark to turn the tide. Feel free to drop us your score predictions in the comments – bragging rights on the line for the winner.

We’ll be bringing you team news, previews from the managers and more ahead of kick-off at 8pm!

Bukayo Saka has once again shown why he is one of English footballâs most admired figures, taking time out to donate over a thousand school uniforms to families struggling with the cost of living crisis.

Hailing from Ealing, Saka gifted the uniforms to four local schools, including Greenford High, where he studied as a youngster.

The Arsenal and England winger visited the school personally to surprise pupils, posing for photos, signing autographs, and helping distribute the uniforms to those in need.

Sources indicate that sharing images of the day on Instagram, Saka wrote: "Special day going back home to launch our school uniform project. Thank you to all the schools, our partners and everybody else who helped us give to the students.".

In 2022, Saka was awarded the Freedom of the Borough of Ealing in recognition of his sporting achievements and his positive influence on young people, following his standout performances at UEFA Euro 2020.

Meanwhile, Outside Greenford High stands a striking mural of Saka, painted in 2021 at the suggestion of a student, celebrating his rise from local schoolboy to football star.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of US artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw their first day of trading on Thursday on the US tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange.

Anthropic is one of the global leaders in AI technology and is best known for its Claude chatbot.

The stock opened at $111.50 (€101.7) — that's 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 and puts the company's valuation at $2 trillion. Anthropic stock ended the first day of trading at $97 per share.

The tech giant's share performance is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

The San Francisco-based manufacturer behind the Claude AI tool has offered 980 million shares at $83 per share, raising a record $81 billion.

This valued the firm at $1.5 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Anthropic is the first big AI tech giant to go public. Its main competitor, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI,  has reportedly pushed its IPO to 2027.

Issuing shares on the stock market is essentially a way to raise money and avoid taking on debt.

Anthropic has already taken on $6.2 billion in debt and is not yet making a profit. At the same time, it faces massive bills for computer power and data centers.

That specific financial situation is one of the reasons for persistent concern that the AI boom might be a bubble that will eventually burst.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal do not traditionally use the January transfer window to do lots of business, but this season may be different.

The Gunners sit pretty at the top of the Premier League table, six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City who sit second and third currently.

But they may look to strengthen their squad when the winter window opens and manager Mikel Arteta is targeting a right-back and a central midfielder.

GIVEMESPORT senior football correspondent Ben Jacobs believes the Gunners will look in the market in January, but may wait until the summer of 2027 to add significantly to their ranks.

Arsenal have suffered with a number of injuries already this season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber missing the start of the campaign, while Bukayo Saka, Martin Zubimendi and more recently David Raya are now sidelined.

Timber has had to cover at centre-back on occasions this season, with Ben White playing at right-back and it is therefore no surprise that they are potentially looking at reinforcements in the full-back area.

And Jacobs has named three potential targets in his exclusive GMS newsletter.

He said: "My information is that Arsenal will be looking for another midfielder, but before we talk about that particular area, we have to think about other pressing positions that Arsenal may focus on.

In a recent development, "As far as the winter is concerned, right-back is relatively high in Arsenal’s thinking, so maybe in the winter, they explore that, if not, it’ll be summer 2027. So yes, midfielder is important, and that is even after the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, but right-back is another area.

It has been revealed that "Arsenal are one of the clubs that have looked historically at Malo Gusto, along with Manchester City and even Manchester United in weeks gone by, but the challenge for all three of these clubs is price. £75million was what Chelsea wanted over the summer. City were maybe the most concrete on Gusto over the summer, but nothing developed, as I say, because Chelsea’s asking price was just a little bit too high.

"You’ve got David Boly and also Ivan Fresneda, two players that are on Arsenal’s radar too, so they’ll be in the market for some form of right-back, for sure.”.

Farm that became a football factory: Club where Man United, Liverpool, Man City, Leeds and Ireland legends started out is back in national Cup final... and hoping it's the first of many more glory days

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:16 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • Gavin Whelan had been away from the domestic game for a while and hadn’t really been looking for a way back in.
  • The former Drogheda United and Bray Wanderers player had stepped away from the League of Ireland at 29 and his involvement in football in the past few years had been restricted to helping coach his older son Jayden’s team as they went through the age grades at Home Farm – the fourth generation of the Whelan family to come through the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:16 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 27 November 2026.

Gavin Whelan had been away from the domestic game for a while and hadn’t really been looking for a way back in.

The former Drogheda United and Bray Wanderers player had stepped away from the League of Ireland at 29 and his involvement in football in the past few years had been restricted to helping coach his older son Jayden’s team as they went through the age grades at Home Farm – the fourth generation of the Whelan family to come through the club.

The Whelan dynasty, with Gavin second from right beside his uncle Ronnie (centre) and Paul (seond from left).

But when it emerged the FAI were setting up a third tier, he had a chat with Brian Honohan, who had been a Shamrock Rovers teammate of his father, Paul, and they decided to put together a group that would help put Home Farm back where they belong.

In a recent development, this inaugural National League final in Carlisle Grounds is a step in that direction. Home Farm face Lucan United, who beat them 2-0 in Whitehall recently in the group stages. In a way, it is like the old meeting the upcoming although the fact that two Dublin clubs are contesting the first final in a concept that was supposed to broaden the league’s base to uncharted territories will be viewed a little sceptically.

But that shouldn’t take away from what both Home Farm and Lucan are trying to do – or the sense of camaraderie and purpose that has characterised the first truncated season of the third tier.

Clubs have become comrades in what they are trying to do – right down to ensuring each visiting team would sit down for a meal after the final whistle before beginning the journey home.

‘There has been a sense that we all have to help each other, that we are all in this together,’ indicates Home Farm chairman Brendan Menton.

Industry observers note that ‘So, the clubs would organise something to eat for the visiting team. It meant that if Bonagee had to go back up the road to Donegal, they wouldn’t need to stop off somewhere. It was a small thing, but it has built a real sense of togetherness among all 15 clubs.’.

Nicola Brannigan (second from left), Brendan Menton (centre), Richard Dunne (second right) and Gavin Peers (right).

Brendan Menton senior was one of the founders of Home Farm back in 1928.

According to recent reports, menton is a former chief executive of the FAI, holding that position during Saipan in 2002. But his footballing roots have been in Home Farm.

Industry observers note that like Whelan, Menton’s family have four generations who have lined out for the famous nursery – with his two grandchildren presently part of the underage teams. And his father, Brendan senior, was one of the founding members of the club back in 1928.

The club came into existence when Leo Fitzmaurice, concerned about the lack of recreational facilities for young people in the Drumcondra and Whitehall area, decided to set up a street league.

Home Farm Road, which is a street in the locality, was one of the roads that formed a team.

‘My father was one of the founding members of the club, who were established to play in the Drumcondra and Whitehall street league. My family lived on 31 Home Farm Road, the name came from a Monastery that was on Iona Road and back a few centuries ago, every Monastery had their own home farm and that’s where the name came from.

‘The story goes that one Friday evening, some boys from the Richmond Road team, which included Don Seery, came to play Home Farm Road but their ball burst so the two teams decided to amalgamate and from that, the club was born.’.

It has been revealed that and from such uncertain beginnings grew one of the most successful schoolboy clubs in Ireland. More than 50 Irish internationals have passed through its famous nursery – from Jackie Carey and Liam Whelan to Gary Kelly and Richard Dunne.

One of the club’s greatest claims to fame was that in the opening game of the 2023 women’s World Cup, two former Home Farm players were on the pitch, one for Ireland and one for Australia – in Abbie Larkin and Mary Fowler, who grew up for a few years in Dublin.

Ireland legends Dunne, Gary Kelly in his Leeds days and inset Jackie Carey, who captained Manchester United.

While it was a schoolboy club nurturing young talent that Home Farm fostered its reputation, it was elected to the League of Ireland in 1972 and three years later achieved its greatest ever success as, in an underdog story to rival Leicester winning the Premier League, they won the FAI Cup.

Menton can still list off the names of all the players for the club’s most famous day in April 1975, including a young Dermot Keely who was in the centre of defence, and Martin Murray, who at 16 was the youngest player to win a FAI Cup medal.

‘Everyone but Jack Dempsey, who was in his late 20s or 30 at the time, was 24 years of age or under. The average age of the team was just 21 and a lot of the players were younger than that, it was an incredible achievement at the time,’ he indicates.

It is that sort of rich and illustrious history that Whelan, Honohan and the other stakeholders want to tap into when they were looking for a pathway back into the league. Home Farm, who had an association with Everton in the latter part of the 1990s, dropped out of the league in 1999 with the franchise being taken up by Dublin City who were eventually subsumed into Sporting Fingal, both now sadly defunct.

The Everton connection came through Martin Murray and saw one of the later graduates of the schoolboy club, Richard Dunne, whose uncle Theo was a coach at Home Farm, go over to Goodison Park as a teenager.

‘I played my schoolboy football at Home Farm and got picked up to go to Everton at 15,’ Dunne remembers.

According to recent reports, ‘We didn’t have the pathway produced by the National League then. And Home Farm was considered the top schoolboy club in Dublin at the time and when scouts and English clubs came over, this was the first port of call. That’s something that probably faded away over time, but hopefully, we can get it back.’.

Team captain Jack Dempsey lifted the FAI Cup for Home Farm back in 1975.

Recent findings suggest that there are around 30 teams at the club now, 10 of them in an underage girls section. The hope is that the likes of Larkin and Fowler can be an inspiration for the next generation.

The club will also move to a new facility in the AUL next summer, as part of the deal that was made when the construction of the Metrolink means that they have to relocate temporarily from their nursery’s home on Mobhi Road in Glasnevin.

They have also got a tie-in with neighbouring Dublin City University, links that the club will hope to deepen. The third-level institution is seen more as a GAA university, but the hope is that they can develop a soccer scholarship programme, so players from the north of the city don’t have to travel to UCD or Shamrock Rovers.

Whelan, who availed of the UCD scholarship, claims it is still in the early stages, but it is one aspect that reveals the ambitions of the club.

Nicola Brannigan, who formerly worked in the FAI marketing department but is now chief executive of the club, claims the relationship has developed through the inaugural season in the national league.

In a recent development, ‘We have students from DCU doing work experience at the club, we have communications students coming in to help us with social media, there is a law student from DCU, so that is one way that the relationship has worked. And then we have a few students or DCU graduates playing for the team,’ she says.

Under former Sligo Rovers star Gavin Peers, who played with the club as a youngster, the senior team have performed above themselves at times this season, but the ambitions are such they always felt they would be in contention to win the inaugural National League.

Sources indicate that but the season has more being about putting Home Farm back on the map. Whelan knows from personal experience what can happen when clubs in the league endure harsh times.

Having scored in the FAI Cup final for Drogheda and winning a league title with them, he was there when things went awry a couple of years later.

Home Farm have not beaten Lucan United so far this season.

‘There was a lot of good people in Drogheda at the time, but it is what can happen when the economy goes south for a club and that is why what we want to build here, we want to do in a conservative and sustainable way and it is why we made sure that the senior club, and the club that we want to eventually get back in the Premier Division, is separate from the schoolboy section.’.

Whelan’s youngest son Sonny is now playing at the under-eight team, the second in a fourth generation of Whelans to pass through Home Farm, stretching back to Whelan’s father Paul and uncle Ronnie and his grandfather, Ronnie senior.

But a greater claim to fame was that Whelan’s goal for Drogheda in 2005 meant that he, his father Paul, who won it with Bohemians, and his grandfather Ronnie senior were the first three generations of the same family  to win a national cup in a European league.

But it all started in Home Farm, which is why he wants to bring the club back to the big-time, especially with the club's centenary coming up in 2028.

‘We want to bring back Home Farm, by using the foundations of what made the club in the past, and its rich history,’ he says.

‘This is where I learned manners, learned discipline, learned teamwork and all of that. The club always had the right ethos and this was just a case of leaving a legacy, showing what the club is and leaving it in a better place.’.

Even though there is no promotion into the First Division this season, it feels like winning the inaugural National League will serve notice of the club’s intention of returning to where they feel they belong.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, our guts contain around 40 trillion bacterial cells, a similar quantity to the number of cells in the entire human body1. Although the community of bacterial species in the human gut usually stays relatively stable over time2, genetic mutations in such bacteria can be associated with a measure of body size called the body mass index3. Writing in Nature, Wang et al.4 scanned the gut bacteria of some 10,000 people for genetic variation and searched for statistically significant associations with almost 250 characteristics, including age, height and cardiovascular fitness. The authors singled out one adaptation that seems to help one of the most abundant bacterial species in the human gut to resist a form of stress called oxidative stress, which damages cells and increases as people age.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Arsenal are not at the moment considering a move for Forbs, despite their recruitment staff being aware of his progress.

The Gunners have reportedly sent scouts to watch Club Brugge on several occasions this season, including their recent Champions League encounter against Liverpool.

Industry observers note that forbs has established himself as an crucial figure at Brugge since joining from Ajax in the summer of 2025. Arsenal’s decision to stay away from Forbs is understandable, considering their existing options in wide attacking positions.

Arsenal could consider bringing in another centre-forward during the January transfer window if a suitable opportunity emerges.

Such an addition could also have implications for Viktor Gyokeres, whose future may come under scrutiny if the Gunners decide to strengthen their attacking department.

For now, Forbs is not understood to be part of Arsenal’s immediate recruitment plans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Climate negotiators have removed any mention of fossil fuels — the main source of greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet — in a fresh draft deal published by COP31 summit co-host Australia.

The latest text released Thursday at the UN climate conference in Turkey stripped out two references to a transition away from coal, oil and gas and a call for an accelerated phaseout that had been in an earlier draft.

This slimmed down version follows days of tough negotiations, with representatives from nearly 200 nations debating issues such as the future of fossil fuels and climate funding for developing countries.

The text still includes a call to increase the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35% by 2035 — up from around 20% today — a proposal that was pushed by host Turkey.

It did not specify whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources rather than fossil fuels, a point that has drawn criticism from some countries.

The draft did mention the electrification target alongside efforts to triple renewable energy capacity globally as well as other energy efficiency measures. But Jan Kowalzig, a climate finance expert with Oxfam Germany, noted negotiators had failed to "meaningfully" link them.

Kowalzig also criticized the text for not referencing a transition away from fossil fuels in a gradual manner — something that had been mentioned in the final decision out of the COP28 in Dubai several years ago.

"This is insufficient for a climate conference that already decided several years ago to phase out fossil fuels and that presents itself as a conference focused on implementation," he remarked in a statement.

Another hotly contested issue at the talks has been financial support to help developing countries deal with climate change. Divisions largely revolve around who should bear the costs and whether funding should come in the form of grants or loans.

It has been revealed that the second draft called for further discussions on a tripling of funding for climate adaptation measures in developing countries. It also noted "with concern the gap between climate finance flows and needs," with the adaptation costs in developing countries estimated at $305 billion annually up to 2035.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The wording on finance prompted criticism from Meenakshi Raman, the coordinator of the climate change program at the Third World Network, who had been "hoping to see much more ambition on the side of finance from the developed world.".

"Coming here really confirmed the worst fears that developed countries are not only backsliding but putting nothing in terms of real meaning on the table," noted Raman.

The European Union has said it won't agree to higher climate financing pledges because it pays its "fair share" while others don't.

The draft text also expressed "deep concern" that global warming is projected to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels — the threshold outlined in the 2015 Paris Agreement to avoid runaway climate change.

It acknowledged that every increment of warming above current levels would "result in increasingly adverse, and in some cases irreversible, impacts and risks to human and natural systems.".

Australian Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen said the text aimed to communicate that "1.5 degrees of warming is not acceptable and will not be allowed to stand.".

The draft also recognized the need for "deep, rapid ​and ‌sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions and called for efforts to ramp up action targeting the potent greenhouse gas methane.

The greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet are largely caused by burning fossil fuels.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The text additionally calls for the deployment of technologies that can remove carbon from the atmosphere to be sped up, many of which have yet to be tested and proven on a large scale.

Harjeet Singh of the Fill the Fund campaign to boost climate finance for developing countries mentioned the second draft "trims away inconvenient mandates and accountability while leaving behind lofty rhetoric that won't protect a single vulnerable community.".

The climate conference officially ends on Friday, but it's not uncommon for the annual talks to run on for longer than expected. The latest text is expected to face further revisions before it can be adopted.

Decisions on the language need approval from all countries, meaning an objection from one party is enough to scupper a deal.

On Thursday, Panama said it would block any agreement that does not meet its demands for a cap on oil production and steps to eliminate methane.

The country's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, noted Panama would "not lend its name" to "complacent or ineffective language" in the final pact.

Australian Energy Minister Bowen stated he expected countries to bring forward their concerns, feedback and questions in the coming hours and overnight.

"We won't be leaving the rooms of Antalya until we have that consensus, until we have a plan we can put to the parties on behalf of the countries and governments they represent, and they can say, yes, we can do this: we can keep the world to 1.5 degrees of warming.".

The stakes are high for this edition of the COP summit, which comes in a year of major climate-related disasters, from wildfires and deadly heat waves in Europe to a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people.

It's also taking place against the backdrop of an intensifying "super" El Nino weather pattern, and geopolitical shocks that have sent energy prices rising globally.

The conference is the first to be held under the acknowledgement by the UN that keeping the average global temperature under 1.5C is no longer realistic. Instead, scientists are talking about limiting the time spent above this threshold and bringing temperatures back down rapidly by the end of the century.

Countries are at odds about how to acknowledge overshoot of the temperature threshold in the final agreement, with some worrying that fossil fuel producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and Iran are seeking to jettison 1.5C entirely, which could lead to "backsliding" on climate action, according to AFP.

"It's critically key for this COP to recognize, and this is really the first COP that will likely do so, that we are on the way to overshooting 1.5 degrees," said David Waskow, the director of the World Resources Institute's International Climate Initiative.

Industry observers note that during the summer, the club were attentive to the situation regarding Lamine Camara, but a deal never materialised for them to make a move. Monaco eventually pulled the plug on his move to Stamford Bridge after the deadline had passed, refusing to put in a deal sheet, and speaking in his latest newsletter, GMS senior correspondent Ben Jacobs has now revealed that there is a chance the Reds make a move in January.

“And then just final word on Lamine Camara, like I stated on deadline day exclusively, Liverpool were calling Camara on deadline day, and they were saying, 'If you don’t go to Chelsea, we could be there for you in 2027'," he said.

"Chelsea were really disappointed by Monaco’s handling there, which means if they are to renegotiate for Camara and move away from Alex Scott, they would likely need Monaco to make a significant concession, and that club-to-club relationship is still very difficult.”.

With lots of interest in Camara during the summer window, Monaco boss Filipe Luis was asked about his midfielder and the speculation around his future, where he admitted that he didn't want to lose him, while calling him 'one of the best midfielders in the world'.

"We are probably talking about one of the best midfielders in the world," he mentioned.

"I don't want to talk about him too much, because I know a lot of clubs would love to have him in their squad, and he is very important to me.

"He has that quality on the ball, covers a lot of ground, he is truly top class! I am really happy to have him, and he is going to play a key role in the team.

"Keeping him? I am very hopeful he will stay. I think he is happy in Monaco. So if he stays, he can play a key role in my game initiative.".

Recent findings suggest that with the Ligue 1 outfit right now struggling domestically this season, it's unlikely that they will want to sell mid-season. However, their financial situation means that a good offer may force their hand, and Liverpool have the cash to spend if they deem it necessary.

These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

It has been revealed that aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

“In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery noted. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

Industry observers note that barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which indicated it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (944 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky.
  • Recent findings suggest that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine.
  • In a recent development, in July, Russia revealed that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky. According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he says, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission.

Recent findings suggest that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine. Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line.

In a recent development, in July, Russia revealed that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine claims the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult.".

Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and said that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city.

Sources indicate that kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.

Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, said Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years.

It has been revealed that local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add thatKostiantynivkahas no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot.

"Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he stated.

Kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian issue for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he said, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity.

Yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and noted the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution.

Kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," remarked Popovych.

After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky, which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition.

Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground.

"If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned.

Popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers right now at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested.

Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population.

The human rights activist mentioned that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said.

This article was originally written in Ukrainian.

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found concern had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

Andoni Iraola says he will not waste any more time thinking about the penalty Liverpool were denied against Arsenal and won’t seek an explanation from Pro Ref. There was a significant fallout following the 1-0 loss at Anfield on Sunday with many judges believing Stuart Attwell, who was VAR, should have consulted match official Andy Madley to highlight an obvious pull by Jurrien Timber that prevented Alexander Isak heading a Bradley Barcola cross.

Liverpool’s head coach explained in the heat of the moment that he would tell his players to go down if they felt contact in the area and Cody Gakpo, the Netherlands international, explained last night in Istanbul it was a message the squad had taken on board.

“As a team, we play pretty fair – maybe we should dive some more like the gaffer said,” Gakpo, who also had claims to be awarded a penalty against Arsenal, explained. “On both occasions you could have given a penalty or a foul, but they decided not. We have to live with the decision. That’s it.”.

But as angry as he was with the situation, Iraola has drawn a line on the matter. He is not going to seek out Pro Ref for a discussion – even though he feels a number of decisions have gone against Liverpool this season – and is channelling his energy into other situations.

It has been revealed that iraola said: “I didn’t ask for an explanation and I haven’t received an explanation, no. I told you what you I think about the plays but, honestly, I don’t have the time to [speak to Pro Ref]. I have been preparing for Fenerbahce. It is just two days between games so I have just been focusing on this game and the opposition and how to prepare the team.”.

Liverpool have made the long trip to Turkey to take on Fenerbahce on matchday four of the Champions League.

Liverpool enter this fixture having won all three Champions League matches thus far, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal to make it nine points from nine for Andoni Iraola’s side. Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

It has been revealed that “Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola mentioned. “It is difficult to find a more crucial night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game. It is very early in the season to establish comparisons. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. Champions League away is very difficult.”.

In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

Fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt has been appointed their interim coach following the resignation of Ismail Kartal following their recent defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray just over a week ago.

“It is a great opportunity for us to show what we can do,” Kuyt said. “It is also a great opportunity for me, a game between two teams that are very vital to me. We have a very good initiative, and we have to believe in this plan. No-one who loves Fenerbahce is happy with the current situation, but this is a huge opportunity. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

They come into tonight’s match having lost back-to-back league games since drawing against Slavia Prague on matchday three of the Champions League. They have plenty of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Ederson, N’Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku.
