England U21s manager Lee Carsley shared his thoughts on Archie Gray with GIVEMESPORT, as the Tottenham midfielder approaches a vital decision about his international career.

Carsley has been busy preparing for next summer's European Championship, as he looks to secure silverware for the third time in charge of the U21s.

Industry observers note that the task ahead has now become even clearer following the official draw. The young Three Lions will square off against France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia in Group A in what Carsley hopes will hand his side a routine entry into the knockout stage.

Just who will be involved in Carsley's squad is now the big question. European football is scattered with top English talents these days and the U21s boss is expected to take full advantage of that.

Carsley spoke to GIVEMESPORT following the draw in Belgrade on Thursday, having his say on several young stars in the process.

The 52-year-old took the opportunity to speak about the likes of Manchester United youngster Ayden Heaven, as well as Gray, who has a particularly vital decision to make in the near future.

The versatile Tottenham star has represented England from U15 to U21 level, but is yet to receive a senior call-up. As long as that is the case, the rules dictate that he will be allowed to represent another national team at senior level as long as he is eligible.

That should offer Scotland some hope. Gray is eligible to play for England's rivals through his father, Andy Gray, who made two appearances for Scotland, his grandfather Frank Gray, who was a European champion with Nottingham Forest and became a star defender with Scotland, and great-uncle Eddie Gray, who also played in front of the Tartan Army.

It's certainly a predicament for the 20-year-old, but he's already had a conversation about his potential England future with Carsley.

Recent findings suggest that "Archie, like a lot of the players, is notable to the Under-21s. He’s got a fantastic history in the pathway, a player that we really enjoy working with. There’s no change to what we spoke about previously.".

The England U21s boss kept his cards close to his chest when it came to the details of that conversation, but Gray is certainly someone that he rates.

In a recent development, whether Thomas Tuchel feels the same way remains to be seen. If the Three Lions are to turn the Spurs man into a fully-fledged England international, then they may have to do so sooner rather than later.

It's not just Carsley who's had his say on Gray's international career. The midfielder, himself, has also commented. He admitted back in 2024 that his desire is to represent England in a major blow for Scotland.

According to recent reports, he told reporters: "My hopes are to play for England, definitely. It’s where I’m from and where I’ve grown up. I’m three quarters English, so that’s where’ I’m at. My dad is totally happy for whatever makes me happy, even though Eddie supports Scotland. But I’m the same as him, I’m happy as long as he’s happy.

"Hopefully I can (get England recognition), but I’ve just got to take it step by step and keep focusing on my club football, which can hopefully attract the attention of whoever it is, whether it’s the Under-21s or it’s the first team. I’d be really happy just to play for my country.".

Whether that lasts the test of time if Gray fails to earn a senior England call-up is the massive unanswered question, however. He certainly wouldn't be the first player to switch allegiances.

Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when world leaders agreed to do what they could to stop the world from overheating back in 2015, it was heralded as a victorious moment. Hope rippled from Paris, where the historic deal was made.

Sources indicate that since then, efforts to curb the use of planet-warming fossil fuels have achieved some success, with coal, oil and gas falling to a record low share of global primary energy supply. But they still account for around 86% of the world's energy.

"We're still burning stuff like [it's] the 19th century," Mark Maslin, professor of Earth System Science at University College London, told DW.

In a recent development, and that has consequences. The United Nations now says overshooting the temperature threshold agreed in Paris 11 years ago is inevitable. That means even more extreme weather events, like storms, flooding, droughts and deadly heat waves and resultant crop failures and water shortages across the world.

The impacts are already being felt globally. This summer, Europe alone recorded 50,000 heat-related deaths in urban areas. In Delhi, India, summer heat waves saw temperatures soar above 45 degrees Celsius (113 Fahrenheit). Even in the relative cool of the evening, there was little respite.

According to recent reports, "It feels like your eyes are burning," remarked Disha Ravi, co-founder of the India chapter of youth climate movement Fridays for Future (FFF). "I always describe it as being cooked alive in an oven.".

Heat waves and other weather extremes are killing people now, says Ravi, and she is aware that as the global average temperature continues to rise, life is only set to become tougher.

"Even at this moment where we haven't even reached the worst of what it could be, it's already difficult," she remarked.

"We should have dealt with climate change 10, 20 years ago," Maslin stated.

The UN now says that the world must keep the time it spends in overshoot as brief as possible, bringing global heating back down by the end of the century.

The longer the planet spends above the threshold, the greater the risk of triggering irreversible, self-perpetuating tipping points, such as massive forest die-back and permafrost melting that would release huge amounts of carbon into the atmosphere.

A recent report by science-based assessment Climate Action Tracker claims limiting overshoot will require policies to rapidly and steeply reduce the emissions warping the climate.

"The stark choice for governments is to continue to support the fossil fuel industry, which would consign humanity to insurmountable economic damages, rising mortality from heat and climate-driven diseases and disasters that they are unable to adapt to — or pivot to the solutions which are available and cheaper than ever," the authors said.

Failure to cut emissions swiftly has made it significantly harder to get climate change under control, and the window for doing so is rapidly closing. But Maslin refers to a Chinese proverb: "When is the best time to plant a tree? Yesterday. When's the next best time to plant a tree? Today.".

Industry observers note that he points to the massive expansion in renewable energy as reason not to despair. Wind, solar and hydropower accounted for around 34% of global electricity production in 2025 and are increasingly being used to meet rising demand.

Last year, record growth in solar power meant that clean energy met all fresh global electricity demand, stifling new fossil fuel generation, according to an analysis by energy think tank Ember.

"At the moment, $2 trillion is being invested in new renewable energy projects around the world, which is twice as much as fossil fuels," Maslin remarked.

But no country is weaning itself off fossil fuels quickly enough to limit the time spent in overshoot. "The transition is happening, it's just not happening fast enough," he added.

One of the problems is that most climate and energy plans focus on building a green energy system rather than creating policy to shift away from fossil fuel use and production, according to a recent report on how to manage the transition by nonprofit research organization, World Resources Institute.

A group of 57 states is working together to manage and accelerate the complicated task of phasing out oil, coal and gas by creating specific roadmaps to do so.

Under the Transition Away from Fossil Fuels initiative (TAFF) initiative, Brazil has published a global roadmap that suggests various measures that can be tailored to each country's financial circumstances and capabilities.

So far, a small but growing number of countries, including Ireland, Denmark, the Netherlands, France, Germany, and Finland, have released national roadmaps.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Yet renewables advocacy group Oil Change International states they largely repackage existing commitments rather than offering new ones, when "what we need is an accelerated timeline for a clean, secure energy system.".

Recent findings suggest that france is sticking to a previously announced deadline of phasing out fossil fuels entirely by 2050. The Netherlands has not published binding dates for quitting oil and gas, and will continue to extract gas in the North Sea.

In a recent development, germany, however, explicitly mentioned transitioning away from fossil fuels by 2045 for the first time, in line with its existing climate neutrality target. The country has also reduced its emissions by 48% compared to 1990 levels.

And while Finland has not set a hard and fast target for phasing out the fossil fuels that still account for 26% of its total energy consumption, it already generates more than 96% of electricity from non-fossil sources.

Industry observers note that "None of these examples is a perfect template," according to the WRI report. "But together, they show that countries are already developing many of the core ingredients of a fossil fuel transition plan.".

Limiting the time spent in overshoot would mean fossil fuel use falling 20% by 2030 and being phased out completely by 2070, according to research institute Climate Analytics.

It also means removing hundreds of billions of tons of CO2 from the atmosphere using carbon removal technologies that remain unproven at scale, as well as nature-based approaches like reforestation.

Sources indicate that and it requires fast action on the short-lived but highly potent greenhouse gas methane. A 45% cut would reduce warming by 0.3%, according to the UN.

Scientists stress that every fraction of a degree matters as the world blows past the threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) of warming above pre-industrial levels. That's because every increment will bring more extreme heat, heavier rainfall, rising seas, and greater and more catastrophic risk for everyone around the world.

Still, even in the face of accelerating climate change, FFF co-founder Ravi rejects the idea that it is too late to act.

"I refuse to believe we'll ever run out of time. No matter how bad it gets," she said. "We owe it to ourselves. We owe it to each other to always try to get out of this mess.".

Ronaldo has revealed that money was the main reason he left Barcelona for Inter in 1997, with the Nerazzurri offering him four times his salary at the Camp Nou.

The Brazilian legend was speaking on the Stick to Football podcast with Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher, in a special episode released today on Disney+.

In a recent development, ronaldo spent just one season at Barcelona after joining from PSV, but it was a spectacular one. He scored goal after goal in La Liga and the Cup Winners’ Cup before Inter paid his release clause to bring him to Serie A.

“Barça bought me for 20 million, and I received a good chunk of that. There, I was earning two million a year, and Inter offered me eight, so I decided to go,” he explained.

Ronaldo said he was still angry about the 1996 Ballon d’Or, when he was voted in second place behind Matthias Sammer.

“I lost it to Sammer, who was a defender. I was angry because I’d played fantastically with Barcelona and scored so many goals,” he mentioned.

Industry observers note that he made up for it in his first season in Milan, winning the Ballon d’Or in 1997 as an Inter player. He won it again in 2002.

Il Fenomeno also suggested modern forwards don’t know how lucky they are.

Sources indicate that “Today’s strikers have an easier life than we did. I’d have liked to have the same protection. We suffered so much. Our generation was full of killers, and nobody protected us,” he said with a laugh.

In a recent development, ronaldo was less upbeat about the Brazil national team. He admitted Argentina’s fighting spirit is “painful” to watch for Brazilians.

According to recent reports, “I think we’re copying European players. Before, there was always very high confidence in our country based purely on our talent. But Europeans today are stronger, faster, more organised, and play better,” he said. “Brazil aren’t strong enough to win the World Cup. We don’t have a strong team, we’re not united.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aerial scenery of Hengqin Free Trade Zone, China. Credit: Weiming Xie/Shutterstock.

Two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in cities by 2050, according to the latest estimates by the United Nations. Coinciding with the mass movement of people into urban areas is the rapid integration of technology into many of those spaces. From automated subterranean waste-collection systems to driverless vehicle zones, these ‘smart-city’ solutions are changing the way that people live, work and move through their environments.

Some cities are embracing these technological advances at a much faster pace than others. Places such as Beijing, Helsinki, London and Singapore stand out for the way they are integrating smart-city technology into existing infrastructure and services.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Other cities are emerging with these technologies integral to their operations from their inception. But as the examples of Songdo in South Korea and Hengqin in China illustrate, building smart infrastructure from scratch is only half the challenge: these places must also attract and retain the research and innovation talent needed to develop, operate and improve it. It’s a ‘chicken-and-egg’ problem, says Songdo-based urban-planning researcher, Dakota McCarty: talent follows world-class universities and thriving economic zones, which need a critical mass of expertise and investment to be attractive.

Real Madrid, Liverpool and Real Betis are the three teams who have the chance to join them on maximum points. Arsenal will jump to 10 points with a win, above Bayern Munich, Sporting and Aston Villa at a minimum.

Slavia Prague are top of the Czech league and unbeaten after 13 games this season, but they are winless in the Champions League after fixtures against Lens, Sabah and Fernerbahce.

The fixture should be a presentable opportunity for Arteta to rotate his team, especially after a physically taxing game at Anfield where Arsenal showed their mettle to win at Liverpool’s home for the first time since 2012.

With fixtures against Manchester City, Borussia Dortmund, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid, Bournemouth and Manchester United before the end of 2026 though, they will not want rush him.

Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Eberechi Eze are other players pushing for greater involvement from the start of matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.

This is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses. In the first nine months of the year, the airline recorded an operating loss of €180 million ($197 million).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, the executive board said on average the loss amounts to €20 million every month, according to media reports. The board stated in the letter that "this is the third year in a row of not being financially successful.".

"Lufthansa is at the moment not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter remarked.

At the end of 2025, the Lufthansa group employed some 67,100 people, up 1% from the previous year.

The tech giant also intends to cut employee travel benefits, restructure its hub operations to reduce crew overnight stays abroad, and reduce short- and medium-haul capacity by replacing some A320 aircraft with A220 jets.

It has been revealed that furthermore, it plans to equip ten aircraft per month with Starlink, a satellite internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. The airline hopes to generate "additional revenue” by monetizing onboard internet access, according to the letter.

According to recent reports, the time frame of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were a part of a previously unveiled downsizing.

In September 2025, Lufthansa remarked it would slash 4,000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

The Preview: Scottish Cup is the perfect proving ground for Clydebank and Co., as band of Lowland League clubs look to make their mark

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 16:44 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • If Clydebank aren’t careful, getting the better of SPFL opposition will soon become something of an expectation rather than a hope.
  • It’s been 23 extraordinary years since its reformation, having gone bust following a series of events which left one of Scottish football’s great clubs — and great communities, for that matter — on its knees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:17 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 16:44 EST, 27 November 2026.

If Clydebank aren’t careful, getting the better of SPFL opposition will soon become something of an expectation rather than a hope. Then again, given their lofty ambitions, that’s exactly the kind of club they want to be.

It’s been 23 extraordinary years since its reformation, having gone bust following a series of events which left one of Scottish football’s great clubs — and great communities, for that matter — on its knees.

That it has taken less than a quarter of a century to get back within touching distance of the SPFL frankly beggars’ belief.

Win the Lowland League West — they right now sit three points behind leaders Largs Thistle with a couple of games in hand — and they will have a crack at earning promotion to the big time via a play-off.

Yet, as exciting a prospect as that may be, it’s something which will be a million miles from the minds of the players, staff and supporters as they rock up at Holm Park this afternoon for a Scottish Cup third-round clash against Championship high-flyers Livingston.

This, of course, is not uncharted territory. Indeed, it’s the third time in as many years that the club have made it to this stage of the competition, and even made it one round further in 2024-25 before bowing out to Hibs at Easter Road.

Clydebank will welcome Championship side Livingston to Holm Park tomorrow.

Yet it wouldn’t necessarily be a great surprise if they were to reach that stage again this time around given the way in which they’ve gone about their business with such professionalism against teams playing much higher up in the football pyramid.

Their incredible run to the KDM Evolution Trophy quarter-finals saw them defeat Dumbarton, East Fife, Kelty Hearts and Alloa Athletic before progressing on penalties against Queen’s Park on Tuesday night.

That win marked the 77th consecutive domestic match in which Clydebank have found the net, incidentally, having surpassed Celtic’s record of 75 set in 2017 a few days earlier.

Recent findings suggest that pulling off a shock once, maybe even twice, could be put down to luck. To do so habitually is something different. Which is why this is a bit of a nightmare draw for Livi.

The days of non-league clubs simply making up the numbers at this point of the competition are a thing of the past, with the gap between the second and fifth tiers of Scottish football seemingly getting smaller with each passing year.

That the likes of Clydebank will genuinely believe they can beat a team chasing an immediate return to the top flight suggests as much.

They are not the only Lowland League West side in action today, with Cumnock Juniors eyeing up a shock as they welcome Championship outfit Arbroath, who know a thing or two about upsetting the odds having punched well above their weight for long enough.

You suspect Raith Rovers won’t be relishing their journey to face Troon at Portland Park, a stadium perhaps best known for hosting a few Brazilian chaps including Pele, Garrincha, Tostao and Zico ahead of the 1966 World Cup in England.

The Lowland League West side have beaten the likes of Alloa and Queen's Park this season.

The names of today’s visitors may not quite carry the same gravitas, but nevertheless, it’s arguably the biggest game in Troon’s 80-year history.

One thing is for certain: there will be at least one Lowland League West club in the hat for the next round, with Renfrew — who have Argyll McCoist, son of Rangers legend Ally in their squad — going head-to-head with Cumbernauld Colts, with both chasing a money-spinning fourth-round tie against one of the country’s massive guns.

Bo’ness United and Brechin City — both battling it out in the Lowland League East this season — are in the same boat ahead of their meeting at Newtown Park.

Fifty miles separate Ross County and Brora Rangers ahead of their clash in Dingwall, but in Highland terms, it constitutes something of a derby.

It has been revealed that the visitors are looking to follow in their opponents footsteps by getting up to the SPFL this season, 22 years after County broke through. And they are going about it the right way too, having gone unbeaten in the Highland League so far this term.

Funnily enough, they are coming against the only other team in Scotland’s top five tiers who share that particular accolade.

And those in charge at Morton will be praying their side can survive their trip to League Two’s basement side Annan Athletic in the hope of pulling a lucrative fixture in the next round.

Amid all the financial uncertainty and concern regarding the future of the Cappielow club these days — even more so following the news earlier this week that main sponsor Dalrada Technology Ltd has been placed in liquidation — goodness knows they need some positivity around the place.

Chelsea slumped to yet another defeat on Friday night, this time at the hands of Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, and Blues fans aren't best pleased with one player in particular.

The West Londoners fell behind after just five minutes when Igor Jesus spectacularly volleyed past Emi Martinez after excellent work from Daniel Munoz down the right. Xabi Alonso's team mustered up just two shots in what was a dire opening 45 minutes from the away side.

Recent findings suggest that forest doubled their advantage shortly after the break when Morgan Gibbs-White sent Martinez the wrong way from 12 yards after Wesley Fofana had clumsily brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea penalty area. The Blues hit back minutes later, with substitute Emanuel Emegha on hand to pounce on a loose ball and slot beyond Matz Sels.

The home team restored their two-goal cushion with 18 minutes left to play, when Gibbs-White added to his tally by clipping the ball over the on-rushing Martinez after Xaver Schlager's exquisite through ball. Emegha pulled one back late on with a neat header, but it wasn't enough for Alonso's men.

The result sees Forest move away from the relegation zone and up into 14th, while Chelsea remain eighth, five points behind Liverpool in fourth.

Alonso's outfit are on a dismal run, losing each of their last three Premier League matches, and fans are subsequently growing frustrated.

While there have been a few murmurings around the manager's future, the focus of Blues supporters' discontent has largely centred around the players.

Fofana, who conceded the penalty that gifted Forest a second goal, was the subject of hostility from the travelling crowd, who booed the Frenchman whilst he was in possession.

However, online, Chelsea fans took aim at a different player. Palmer, who created just one chance and took no shots on the night, was heavily scrutinised by his own supporters on social media.

One fan bluntly wrote on X: "Cole Palmer. What a waste of space.".

"Cole Palmer has actually fallen off a cliff, what am I watching here?" another added.

Meanwhile, one fan had a team selection suggestion for Alonso, urging him to drop Palmer for the next game and start Estevao instead.

"Palmer needs to be benched for a game at this point. Let Estevao fight for his spot.".

Industry observers note that "What happened to Palmer? He looks to have lost his attacking prowess," another wrote.

This theme continued, with another fan stating that the playmaker is 'a shadow of himself' and another accusing the player of 'ghosting again'.

Meanwhile, two more roped Morgan Rogers into the criticism.

"Rogers & Palmer, I have no words for you both," one posited.

Finally, a supporter described the pair's displays as 'pathetic': "Palmer and Rogers have been pathetic.".

In a recent development, what makes Palmer special when he's performing at his best level is his ability to create chances and get shots off from difficult positions. Against Forest, he did neither.

He played within himself, opting against risky moves in the final third and instead choosing to retain possession. Creating one chance, taking no shots and completing just two dribbles, it was a completely ineffective performance from the number ten.

Expected Goals + Expected Assists.

Recent findings suggest that alonso has tasked the England international with dropping deep from time to time to help Chelsea progress the ball. He did this relatively well at the City Ground, completing nine line-breaking passes, but this came at the expense of his influence in the final third.

While Palmer must step up and take more responsibility, his coach needs to concoct a system that elicits more from his star attacker.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
  • Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era.
  • Sources indicate that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

Sources indicate that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

At the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

Infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is mentioned to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment proposal, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

However, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

It has been revealed that "We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Recent findings suggest that diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he stated.

Sources indicate that "Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

According to recent reports, but he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo remarked he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he said.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

#164403. From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap

📅 28 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (997 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (997 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that artificial-intelligence tools can speed up the process of generating publication-ready flowcharts.
  • When making a scientific diagram, whether I am outlining a clinical study, planning a flowchart or mapping a signalling pathway, I often start in the same way: with a pen and a piece of paper.
  • Recent findings suggest that sketching by hand is fast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that artificial-intelligence tools can speed up the process of generating publication-ready flowcharts. Credit: -MG-/Getty.

When making a scientific diagram, whether I am outlining a clinical study, planning a flowchart or mapping a signalling pathway, I often start in the same way: with a pen and a piece of paper.

Recent findings suggest that sketching by hand is fast. I can draw a box, cross something out and reorganize a whole idea without thinking about fonts, alignment or software menus. At this stage, my aim is not to make the figure beautiful, it is to work out the logic.

Industry observers note that turning that rough sketch into a clean figure for a manuscript can be surprisingly tedious, however. Text boxes need to line up; arrows need to connect properly; and fonts, spacing and colours must be consistent. A diagram that took five minutes to draw might take an hour or longer to recreate digitally.

Industry observers note that multimodal artificial-intelligence tools can shorten this process. Rather than asking an AI model to create the final scientific image, I use it as a translator. The model reads my sketch, interprets its structure and converts it into editable diagram code that I can open in a vector-based editor, such as Draw.io — a free application for making diagrams.

This distinction matters. I do not want AI to invent a figure for me; I want it to help me to digitize a figure that I have already designed.

One tempting approach is to provide a description to an image-generation model and ask for a polished scientific figure.

Recent findings suggest that for research diagrams, this can create more problems than it solves. Text might be misspelt, arrows misdirected and pathways altered. More importantly, the resulting image is usually flat (that is, the text, images and background are merged together), making it mostly uneditable. For diagrams in research publications, if a reviewer later asks you to alter it, you might have to start from scratch.

A better option is to ask a multimodal language model — for example, Google’s Gemini — to turn your idea into a structured diagram format, such as Draw.io-compatible XML or Mermaid syntax. The output can then be imported into a diagram editor, in which every box, label and connector remains editable.

In this workflow, AI is less an illustrator than a compiler: a programming tool that translates human-readable instructions into code that a computer can run. My sketch is the source, and Draw.io XML is the output.

Focus first on the structure of your figure. I roughly sketch the vital nodes, branches and connections without worrying about visual polish. For a clinical study, these might include eligibility criteria, treatment groups and follow-up visits. For a laboratory workflow, they might represent experimental stages or decision points.

The key is to make the relationships clear. What box comes first? Where does the pathway split? Which arrow connects to which endpoint? If the logic is ambiguous to a human reader, it will be ambiguous to the AI model, too.

Industry observers note that once the sketch is complete, I photograph it, upload the image to a vision-enabled language model and provide a detailed prompt. For instance:.

In a recent development, “Recreate the uploaded hand-drawn figure as a clean, editable academic flowchart in Draw.io-compatible XML format. Preserve the original structure as faithfully as possible, including box positions, arrows, dashed connectors, side boxes, branching pattern, and text content. This is a reconstruction task, not a redesign task. Use a plain white background, thin dark slate-grey borders, white box fills, thin connector lines, clean sans-serif text, and no shadows, gradients, or decorative elements. Make it publication-quality while keeping it recognizably the same diagram.”.

The instruction “This is a reconstruction task, not a redesign task” is crucial. Scientific diagrams are not the place for creative completion. I want the model to reconstruct my structure, not improve it on my behalf.

In a recent development, note also that this prompt indicates what the model should not change. I explicitly ask it to preserve wording, branching relationships and directionality. If the diagram contains important numbers, doses or time points, I check each one manually.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03513-1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toni Kroos has revealed his belief that Arsenal only have two 'world-class' players in their midst, and Declan Rice isn't one of them.

In a recent development, mikel Arteta's men won the Premier League title last season and were only denied a historic double by a penalty shootout, losing on spot-kicks to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final in Budapest in May. The Gunners are on course to retain their crown as champions of England, as they right now sit six points clear, while many have tipped them to go all the way in Europe's elite club competition this term.

The North Londoners boast an embarrassment of riches across the pitch, with this deep and talented squad ultimately leading to all this success.

Despite this, six-time Champions League winner Kroos doesn't think there are more than two world-class players in Arteta's squad.

World-class has made its way into football's lexicon and is now considered an exclusive bracket of players that only the very elite on the planet fit into. However, a universal definition has never been established, despite many people arguing effusively whenever someone makes a claim about a player being world-class or not being world-class.

Ultimately, it can be assumed that the best teams in Europe all contain a multitude of world-class players, although Kroos doesn't believe so.

Speaking in an interview with Luppen TV, the former Real Madrid midfielder named David Raya and William Saliba as Arsenal's sole 'world-class' players, snubbing Rice in the process.

"I’m also in agreement that Arsenal are a world-class team for me, but not one studded with tons of world-class players,” he said.

Kroos added that he agreed with compatriots Mats Hummels and Kramer's take on Prime that Saliba is 'absolutely world-class', before disagreeing with the pair, who claimed that the Frenchman is the only Gunners player who falls into this category: “So, I’m not quite there, because I think, for example, Raya is also a world-class goalkeeper.".

Asked about Rice and Martin Odegaard, the German stated the pair are 'a bit behind that, but not as absolute world-class'.

"I believe that it is a world-class team in how they play together and how they function together. They’ve shown that.”.

Just last month, Rice was nominated for the Ballon d'Or, with the only other midfielders who were up for the award being Rodri, Fabian Ruiz, Jude Bellingham, Vitinha, Joao Neves and Bruno Fernandes.

Clearly, the general perception is that Rice is among the best few players in his position in the world, which would qualify him for a 'world-class' tag in many people's eyes.

Equally, Gabriel Magalhaes was also nominated for the Ballon d'Or, and was also snubbed by Kroos, while Bukayo Saka wasn't mentioned at all by the legendary deep-lying playmaker.

He's savoured silverware, snubbed the 49ers and set Derek McInnes on the path to managerial success... but all former St Johnstone chairman Geoff Brown wanted was to make the people of Perth proud

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that geoff Brown walked into his home more than 70 years ago to a mother crying because she feared she could not put bread on the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:30 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 17:32 EST, 27 November 2026.

The child is the father to many traits that inhabit the man.

Sources indicate that geoff Brown walked into his home more than 70 years ago to a mother crying because she feared she could not put bread on the table. Now, at 83, he knows that his children, grandchildren and great grandchildren will never suffer that anguish.

It has been revealed that he was a child who lived in a cramped house with the family of eight at one time sharing three rooms. He made his business by building large family homes and constructing a huge one for himself.

Sources indicate that he was a football player and coach in his childhood and as a young adult. He then bought a football team as a successful businessman and his unflinching tenure ensured it would survive and then prosper. He was born in St Johnstouns Nursing Home in 1943 and later would own St Johnstone.

According to recent reports, as a child, too, he had a working horse, Prince. As a multimillionaire, he had a string of racehorses. He now focuses on providing horses and hosting events for Riding for the Disabled.

The foundations of his future were laid in his childhood.

Geoff Brown was chairman at St Johnstone for 38 years and retains a deep bond with the club.

The most public achievement is his stewardship of St Johnstone. The club, simply, would not be still playing if Brown had not stepped in and run it for 38 years.

‘If I knew then what I later knew then I would never have got involved,’ he says briskly of his takeover in 1986. ‘No one would have touched St Johnstone with a bargepole.’.

Sources indicate that brown, then, has lived a full life but its broad scope can shimmer with odd, illuminating moments. His conversation is serious but never dull. He tells of how the mobile phone bill of Derek McInnes was evidence he was an excellent manager, how his grandmother was his driving force, and how football made him indulgent without measure.

He sets out his philosophy in simple terms. The son of a struggling market gardener, he indicates: ‘People are what matter. All my life I have wanted to provide for my family.’.

The Browns, with six children, lived in a house with no bathroom. There were two bedrooms for the children. The parents slept in the living room.

‘Even today, at the age of 83, I have a vivid memory of being 10 years old and seeing my mother in tears because we didn’t have money for bread.’.

Brown and his son Steve, who took over as chairman, celebrate double cup success in 2021.

The teenage Brown left school, became a joiner, started a business and built a portfolio of interests that all stemmed from his hard work and ability to make a deal.

Sources indicate that he insists his greatest skills are ‘to be observant and have commonsense’. The first trait is exemplified by his aside when assessing his former manager, McInnes.

‘His phone bill during the summer was twice as much as any other manager we ever had,’ he says.

‘What does that tell you? Yes, he was working away trying to get players in and seeing what was going on. He never stopped.

Sources indicate that ‘Football is gossip. If you know what is going on then you are a step ahead. Derek was ready on day one of the season.’.

Sources indicate that paul Sturrock, a firm friend, remains his favourite Saints manager but his appraisal of McInnes is stunning. Asked about the task at Rangers, he notes: ‘I don’t see another manager in Scotland who could do the job he will do. He has a positive mindset. He makes decisions and then gets on with it.’.

According to recent reports, there is more than a bit of that in Brown’s personality. ‘Yes, I never had five-year plans or any ultimate strategy,’ he indicates. ‘I just get up in the morning and deal with what is in front of me.’.

Brown is full of admiration for the managerial talents of Derek McInnes, whom he hired in 2007.

This energy took him to St Johnstone. He made it clear from his first interest in the club that he was not going to be a collegiate manager. Brown was going to run it his way. ‘There was no way I was going to become involved unless I had complete control,’ he writes in his autobiography.

In a recent development, the club’s substantial debts emerged quickly. ‘I hadn’t seen the books and the directors hadn’t told me how bad things were. It soon became clear what a mess the club was in financially.’.

He wrote a cheque for £100,000 immediately. ‘Aye, if I knew then what I know now…’.

Sources indicate that his decades at the helm of St Johnstone, in bad times and in glorious moments, have given him stark lessons. ‘With football it is money, money, money,’ he says.

Recent findings suggest that the commonsense, he admits, was an early casualty. He had promised the players a communal bonus of £250,000 if they finished fourth and gained European competition in the 1998/99 season.

It has been revealed that ‘They then asked for £500,000 if they finished third and I stated: “Okay, they will never do that”. Of course, they did and then we made nothing near that in Europe.’.

Brown looks out over the club's old Muirton Park home before the move to McDiarmid Park.

In the qualifying round for the UEFA Cup, the Saints beat Finnish side VOS but were beaten in the first round proper by Monaco.

‘I felt I was too soft in football,’ says Brown, ‘As I say, it was all about money and people can get swept along.’.

He sidesteps any praise for the Scottish Cup win in 2014 and the domestic cup double in 2021, pointing out they occurred under the reign of his son, Steve. He pays tribute, too, to Stewart Duff, who was a stalwart as managing director in those times.

Yet Brown was a constant presence and a huge influence at the club until he sold it to Adam Webb in 2024. The deal was done on a handshake and Brown later learned that the 49ers group, who subsequently took over Rangers, were keen to talk. ‘There were no discussions,’ he says. ‘I shook Adam’s hand and a deal is a deal. I would not have talks with anyone else once I had given my word.’.

In a recent development, he adds: ‘One thing is odd, though. Adam had to give up his share in Cambridge before the SFA would allow him to progress with the deal. Yet the 49ers still have a share in Leeds.’.

It has been revealed that he worries about Scottish football. ‘It’s difficult for clubs. They are all in tough positions,’ he states. This is primarily in reference to finances but he has deep concerns about the dearth of young players coming through.

Brown with new club chairman and owner Adam Webb, who bought the Perth outfit in 2024.

Asked what he would do first if he was at the Scottish Football Association, he answers quickly: ‘I would reintroduce primary school football. That is where all the great players learned. I ran an under-13 team at St Madoes and that was the progression for primary schools.

It has been revealed that ‘The club academies have not worked. Players are rejected too early and for the wrong reasons. Someone who is small at ten can be tall at 15. Players progress at different rates and once there was that path from school to boys’ club to Juniors or above.’.

The problem is visible. ‘I watched three games recently: Switzerland v Scotland, Wales v Portugal and Motherwell v Rangers. Wales were much better than us, good to watch. In the Motherwell game, there was not a single Scottish player on the park,’ he indicates.

Industry observers note that he has other interests to comfort him. He is a keen golfer and does a bit of shooting. He also has retained his interest in horses. He no longer has thoroughbreds in training but has devoted time and money for disabled people, particularly children, having a place to ride horses.

In 2014, he created a charity and refurbished a large barn at Castle Farm, Kinfauns, to be fully compliant with the needs of Riding For the Disabled.

‘It’s been a great success,’ he says.

Brown proudly shows the Princess Royal around his Kinfauns stable in Perthshire in 2016.

He and his family never took a wage out of St Johnstone. The money for the riding at Castle Farm is generated by Brown. The horses are his.

So what was his reward for decades in sport? Was it the joy of being in control at a football club?

‘No, that was a bit of a bind, to be honest. It took far more time out of my life than I ever thought,’ he says.

But surely providing pleasure to generations of Saints fans, giving them days of glory in finals and seeing them play in Europe, that must mean something?

‘The thing I have always wanted was to give something back to the people of Perthshire,’ he indicates. But he does not expand.

Horses have played a central role in Brown life and he helps run Riding for the Disabled charity.

In the book there is a poignant scene of Brown watching a disabled girl being helped from a horse back into her wheelchair.

‘Aye, I always remember her smile,’ he states to me. ‘That is payment in full.’.

Geoff Brown: always observant but blessed with more than commonsense.

Breaking: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (782 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
  • A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • In a recent development, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last significant media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a recent development, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

The broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a fresh account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

The Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

In a recent development, according to the investigators, Akbay is said to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

Industry observers note that it is not new for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

It has been revealed that sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

In the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

In a recent development, esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen says Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Recent findings suggest that esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he says, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Industry observers note that several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and revealed its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, showed how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

"These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

This article has been translated from German.

Once that mountain peak arrives, however, the only way is down and the sightseeing opportunities rapidly turn into dangerous cliff edges. The glory is so often torn down quicker than it had originally been built up.

Sources indicate that the likes of Raheem Sterling and Dele Alli have fallen by the wayside in recent years. Sterling went from glory at Manchester City to struggles at Arsenal and Chelsea, before pleading guilty to dangerous driving and nitrous oxide offences in 2026 and receiving a 12-month suspended sentence.

According to recent reports, alli was tipped to be the next best thing by many. In 2026, he is a free agent and has turned to Twitch streaming.

Both are devastating cases with their own story, which have followed a similar path to Anthony Stokes' dramatic fall from grace.

According to recent reports, stokes had the world at his feet at just 14 years old when he completed a move to Arsenal from Shelbourne in 2003. He very much looked destined to become the next massive Irish talent, especially after a loan spell with Scottish side Falkirk ended with 14 goals in 16 appearances three years later.

It has been revealed that what followed should have been his rise to the top. Instead, the striker's career began to suffer a dramatic fall off - starting with a difficult move to Sunderland.

Industry observers note that after arriving for £2m, Stokes failed to live up to expectations and scored just three goals in 36 appearances. Loan moves to Crystal Palace and Sheffield United then failed to revive his career in English football and a return to Scotland followed.

It has been revealed that it was there that Stokes found his feet again, scoring 22 goals in 44 games for Hibernian and then racking up 135 appearances for Celtic and scoring a further 58 goals. Alas, that would be as good as it would get for the forward, who went onto score a total of just 25 goals for his next nine clubs.

Stokes' failed potential will hurt him more than anyone else, especially after Celtic where he was teammates with Virgil van Dijk and finally at his best.

What followed a disappointing career was even more devastating than the career itself. In 2024, Stokes pleaded guilty to unlawful possession of cocaine at the value of £3.1k, which had been hidden in a sock, and having the drug for sale or supply.

The former Arsenal prospect also admitted driving while over the alcohol limit and four counts of dangerous driving, as well as not producing a driving licence and not having motor insurance.

It has been revealed that stokes originally received a 15-month sentence with a five-year road ban, before an appeal spared him prison time altogether. Judge Jonathan Dunphy instead ordered a suspended sentence and 240 hours of community service, claiming that the former Premier League forward had "a lot to offer once he sorts out his difficulties.”.

The court heard that Stokes' drinking problem started during his playing days after "too much too soon" as a young prospect, who uprooted his life to join Arsenal at just 14.

After the incident, Stokes signed for a pub team for Conor McGregor’s Black Forge Inn boozer, returning to football outside a professional level for the first time since 2020.

Milan have rekindled their interest in Fenerbahçe left-back Archie Brown as they consider their options on the left flank.

Sources indicate that according to MilanNews24, the Rossoneri are studying the Englishman’s situation again, more than a year after he turned them down. Brown chose Fenerbahçe over Milan in July 2025, when the Turkish club bought him from Gent for €8 million and signed him until June 2028, with an extra year as an option.

His contract includes a release clause of around €23m, which can be triggered in either January or next summer. That gives any interested club more flexibility.

Recent findings suggest that the 24-year-old has become a regular starter in Istanbul and has impressed in the Champions League. Several Premier League clubs have already enquired about him, so the Rossoneri could face serious competition.

Industry observers note that his name is back on Milan’s list because of uncertainty over Pervis Estupiñán, whose agent, Jorge Mendes, is exploring possible destinations for the Ecuadorian. For now, though, the Rossoneri are only monitoring the situation, and no formal offer has been made.

Brown came through Derby County’s academy before spells at Lausanne-Sport and Gent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham noted.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He mentioned jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Burnham said that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and said "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up latest opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen said the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She mentioned the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also stated Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham remarked the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham noted he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

"Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham stated as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

Sources indicate that no deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on complications including on tuition fees," Burnham said.

Von der Leyen ‌mentioned ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

On the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders noted they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club.
  • It has been revealed that spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation.
  • The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club. It is a legal win for the two clubs, but the later December 2021 approval behind LALIGA Impulso remains in force.

It has been revealed that spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation. The General Assembly resolution of 12 August 2021, which approved the deal, therefore stays void for good. Real Madrid and Athletic Club brought the winning case. LaLiga now carries the costs of the failed appeal.

The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote. In August 2021, Barcelona, Athletic Club and Real Madrid jointly revealed a challenge to the resolution. They argued it broke Royal Decree-Law 5/2015 and was passed through a highly irregular process.

Sources indicate that real Madrid described the annulled resolution as one of huge economic significance. In the club’s account, it was passed before clubs had enough information to judge the scope, impact and consequences of changes to the operation. The club also highlighted the court’s remark that LaLiga’s appeal tried to replace the Provincial Court’s view with LaLiga’s own self-interested view.

LaLiga reads the decision more narrowly. The annulled assembly approved the term sheet of the CVC project, and the appeal fell for lack of cassation interest. LaLiga noted the court issued a procedural order rather than a judgment endorsing the Provincial Court’s reasoning, and did not examine the substance of the case.

It has been revealed that the deal itself does not depend on the annulled vote. LaLiga’s General Assembly approved the LALIGA Impulso project later, on 10 December 2021. Under the deal, clubs received around €2bn in exchange for a share of the value of the competition’s audiovisual rights over 50 years. A fresh company set up by LaLiga and the fund manages that arrangement. Real Madrid, Barcelona and Athletic Club rejected it and stayed out.

Those December resolutions have survived their own court test. In June 2026, Section 18 of the Madrid Provincial Court rejected in full the appeal by Athletic Club and Real Madrid against them. It upheld the first-instance judgment of 19 February 2024 and ordered both clubs to pay the costs of that hearing. The court found that clubs still own their audiovisual rights, while LaLiga sells them collectively under the law. It also ruled that creating LaLiga Group International, owned jointly by LaLiga and CVC, did not breach the Sports Law or LaLiga’s statutes.

In a recent development, that leaves the practical picture largely unchanged. Iusport, a Spanish sports-law outlet, described the Supreme Court order as having no practical effect on the LaLiga–CVC deal. The ruling still matters for how LaLiga is run, because it confirms that one of its assembly votes on the operation was unlawful. The league insists it respects court decisions and will keep defending the agreements backed by most of its clubs.

In a recent development, dortmund have never fought harder for a player in recent years than Bellingham. The club’s executives first met him in person in the summer of 2020, when Jude signed. Jobe accompanied his brother to Germany. From that moment on, the club monitored every step of his development: his progress through the youth ranks at Birmingham City, the family club of the Bellinghams, and the evolution of his positioning on the pitch. After all, as a child, Jobe was still playing as a centre-forward. Over time, however, he gradually moved into deeper roles.

Sources indicate that in May 2025, BVB decided to make their move. Word had reached Dortmund that Eintracht Frankfurt were interested and had already invited Bellingham to their training facilities. The pressure was on. Dortmund responded by pulling out all the stops. President Hans-Joachim Watzke, the man who shaped the club for more than two decades and led it to the top of German football, stepped in. He flew to England and met Bellingham face to face. It was a secret mission. Watzke was determined not to attract any attention that could jeopardise negotiations.

Recent findings suggest that the problem: Sunderland, Bellingham’s former club, had secured promotion to the Premier League only a day earlier. Hundreds of supporters were gathered outside the hotel where Watzke and Bellingham were due to meet. To avoid being recognised, Watzke put on sunglasses and a cap before making his way through the crowd. He brought two gifts with him. Firstly, a BVB shirt with Jobe’s name on the back. Secondly, a handwritten note from Kovac expressing his desire to work with the midfielder. A few days later, Watzke received a phone call. It was Jobe. His decision had been made. He was joining Dortmund.

Recent findings suggest that ever since, the midfielder has enjoyed almost unwavering support. Watzke frequently spoke with him throughout his first season, offering encouragement and reassurance. The same was true of Kovac and other senior figures. Equally important to his breakthrough has been team-mate Felix Nmecha, with whom Bellingham has developed a close friendship and who has become an important source of advice. When time allows, the two enjoy playing padel together. Off the pitch they are opponents; on it they form a midfield partnership.

And while his father Mark was still complaining to club officials around a year ago that his son was not getting enough playing time, the situation has changed dramatically. The Bellingham family are delighted, and his England call-up has provided further confirmation that he is on the right path.

Thomas Tuchel has Jordan Henderson back fit – and playing well – since the last international break. From Tuchel’s squad in the summer, Djed Spence has also returned from injury although he is only just back playing for Inter Milan.

Marcus Rashford is set to miss out on England through injury having barely played since the last international break. The Manchester United forward pulled out of the last squad, then returned for his club the following weekend. But he has not featured since the defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. England have already qualified for the knockout phase – barring a defeat by Croatia by a margin of eight or more goals – but would need two victories to avoid France and Portugal in the next two-legged phase in March.

Tuchel’s only major injury doubt from the last squad are Arsenal’s Bukao Saka and Como’s Trevoh Chalobah as well as the more long-term absentee Tino Livramento, the man Chalobah replaced in the World Cup 26. Djed Spence has returned to full fitness and played for Inter in their Milan derby defeat last weekend while the head coach’s favourite player, Jordan Henderson, has been passed fit to play for Chelsea at his boyhood club Sunderland on Sunday though at 36 his race may finally have been run at this level despite his unexpected encore in the last 18 months.

For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

Whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant glitch of note. The Chelsea forward pulled out of the last squad as part of his club’s management of his groin injury but he has played in their last four Premier League games, scoring once and being sent off once as well. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

The squad will be released at 10am and followed by Tuchel’s explanations, which we will also cover here, an hour later.

Newcastle are being tipped to solve their goalscoring challenges this winter with a move to bring Ivan Toney back to St James’ Park.

It is a transfer which would reunite the England international with former boss Matthias Jaissle, with whom he worked at current club Al-Ahli.

Finding the back of the net has proved a major headache for Jaissle since taking the reins on Tyneside and following a summer exodus that stripped the Magpies of their spine, none of Newcastle’s current central striking options have managed to nail down a starting spot in his team.

It has been revealed that will Osula and Yoane Wissa have mustered just a single league goal apiece so far this campaign, while Matias Fernandez-Pardo is still waiting to open his account. Without a reliable penalty-box presence, Jaissle’s side have lacked a cutting edge in the final third.

Toney thrived under Jaissle during their time together in Saudi Arabia. The former Brentford frontman has been expectedly prolific in the Middle East, netting 87 times in 110 appearances across all competitions.

Any transfer negotiations may even be smoothed over by shared ownership links, as both Al-Ahli and Newcastle are majority-owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Despite his form in the Saudi Pro League, Toney has slipped down the international pecking order and missed out on recent England squads, a setback that is expected to spark a push for a Premier League return in the Latest Year.

Speaking on the Everything is Black and White Podcast, The Chronicle’s chief Newcastle reporter Lee Ryder suggested the 30-year-old will be chomping at the bit to head back to English football.

A switch to St James’ Park would see Toney return to the club he departed almost a decade ago. Newcastle originally signed the striker from Northampton Town over in 2015, but made just two Premier League outings before being sent out on a series of loans. Spells at Barnsley, Shrewsbury, Scunthorpe and Wigan followed, before he was eventually sold to Peterborough United in 2018.

Having since proved his top-flight pedigree at Brentford, Toney would bring additional physicality and an aptitude for finishing that Newcastle are presently missing.

  • Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men. The victory keeps their cup run alive ahead of the second-round draw.

At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

Recent findings suggest that carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

Jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

According to recent reports, the Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

Tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

In a recent development, this was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

In a recent development, the second round will feature 56 teams in 28 one-off ties. The lower-division side hosts if its ground meets federation standards. KASPER HOGH - THE £11M ENIGMA: Until such time as Celtic can cut their losses on the misfit striker, Martin O'Neill has a problem on his hands
