📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 14:08 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • On the website of Pluto Data Analytics, prospective clients are given a taste of what they can expect if they form a partnership with the London-based firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EST, 27 November 2026.

On the website of Pluto Data Analytics, prospective clients are given a taste of what they can expect if they form a partnership with the London-based firm.

Under a section headed ‘Transferability You Can Trust,’ football clubs are told: ‘At Pluto, we use advanced machine learning to validate how a player might adapt in a newly introduced league.

It has been revealed that ‘For example, how would a defender in Japan’s J1 League perform in the MLS in America? This kind of insight supports clubs to make smarter, more confident recruitment decisions across borders.’.

We’ll never know, of course, how different Celtic’s summer transfer dealings might have been had they got into bed with the firm before this week.

But on one question, in particular, the Parkhead club would have been likely to have seen more red flags raised than a communist parade.

‘How would a forward who’s so clearly tailor-made for a unique environment north of the Arctic circle fare in the Scottish Premiership?’ Well, not too great, as it turns out.

Hogh endured another tough night in Portugal as his goalless run extended to 17 games.

Listen, you didn’t need to have a PhD in mathematics to question the wisdom of Celtic paying a record £11million to sign Kasper Hogh from Bodo/Glimt in the summer. Just an appreciation that so many players who’ve thrived at that extraordinary club have found success hard to come by elsewhere.

Industry observers note that this observation is hardly new. It’s been the subject of discussions throughout Europe since the impressive Kjetil Knutsen began establishing a culture at the Norwegian outpost in 2018, one which would pave the way to four titles, a cup and a run to the semi-finals of the Europa League.

Recent findings suggest that knutsen and his sizeable entourage have created a world of their own 520 miles north of Oslo. And the dogs in the street know that those who venture outside it rarely do well.

It has been revealed that sure, Victor Boniface, now of Bayer Leverkusen, hasn’t really looked back since leaving for Union Saint-Gilloise. And Hugo Vetlesen has done well since moving to Club Brugge two years ago.

But they are outnumbered by those who looked lost the minute Bodo/Glimt sold them. Patrick Berg, Fredrik Bjorkan and Jens Petter Hauge, to name but three.

Sources indicate that were Celtic not aware of this curious trend as Bodo/Glimt somehow convinced them to part with a club-record fee? Or did their research only go as far as the five goals Hogh scored in the Champions League last season?

Provided this Tuesday’s annual general meeting does not descend into disarray, an explanation from someone involved in the deal would be fitting.

Hogh wasn’t some six-figure punt, after all. He was an eight-figure sure thing. Or, at least, that’s what the Celtic hierarchy believed him to be.

It has been revealed that who first flagged him up and who agreed that he was worthy of such a gargantuan investment? The trouble with Celtic these days is that no one is quite sure about who’s responsible for that kind of thing.

Despite Paul Tisdale leaving his head of football operations post on January 5, the club has yet to appoint a replacement. Nor has the vacant role been reclassified to that of director of football or sporting director.

Industry observers note that two months previously, chief scout Jay Lefevre left for Swansea. Despite Mark Cooper effectively filling that void and former Chelsea operative James Bell-Walker joining the team in January, officially, there is still no head of recruitment.

O'Neill turned to Columbian hitman Duran to get Celtic out of a hole against Torreense.

That’s just not a good look when the collective decision in June was to go all-in on a player who’s now gone 17 games without a goal.

Industry observers note that celtic’s partnership with the analytics manufacturer is all well and good and may indeed sharpen up the club’s future recruitment. It certainly needs it.

But it can’t undo what’s already done. And until such time as the club can cut its losses on Hogh and sign a replacement, Martin O’Neill has a serious problem on his hands.

Starting at Tynecastle tomorrow and up to the visit to Ibrox on January 3, Celtic have eight games to play.

That run includes a trip to Cyprus to face Omonia Nicosia, which now carries added significance after Thursday’s narrow win over Torreense revived the club’s Europa League hopes.

The trouble is that Hogh can no longer be trusted to deliver in any of those crucial matches. That much became abundantly clear across his dismal 59-minute contribution in Portugal.

That old cliché about strikers always being judged on goals has never actually rang true. Provided they hold the ball up and facilitate their team-mates to score, there will always be a degree of forgiveness.

It has been revealed that hogh’s epic goalless run stretching back to the hat-trick he hit at Kilmarnock on August 9 is only one part of the story now. It’s his inability to do the fundamentals of football — securing possession and finding a man — which have taken him to the point of no return.

This is no longer about one man needing a scruffy goal to get going. That’s just not going to happen. He’s demonstrably the wrong fit for Celtic. He has been a scandalous waste of money.

In a recent development, his display against Torreense was that of a player who is getting worse by the week, not better. He touched the ball just 13 times, misplaced three passes and only found a team-mate on seven occasions.

In a recent development, hogh’s one moment of promise came when he robbed veteran defender Stopira in the right channel just before half-time. Having done the hard part and got to the line, his cut-back went straight into the goalkeeper’s arms.

Hogh's confidence already looks shot after making a miserable start to his Celtic career.

‘It’s poor. It’s really poor. He is really lacking conviction,’ said former Celtic manager Neil Lennon.

Hogh’s withdrawal came not a moment too soon for the visiting fans. With approximately half as much time on the pitch, his replacement, Camilo Duran, managed just one touch fewer than the Dane, including the header for the winning goal which came from James Forrest’s cross.

In a recent development, now with 15 goals for the season after signing from Qarabag for an initial £4.5m, the Colombian is continuing to prove that spending money is one thing. It’s how you spend it which is crucial.

O’Neill is hardly without options across the front area as a defining spell begins in Gorgie.

Sources indicate that after being sidelined for 18 months with a serious knee injury, Jota’s display against Torreense was scintillating. There should be no concerns now over the £8m which was spent to bring him back to the club.

While Yang Hyun-jun had a poor night in Portugal, it was a rarity in recent times. The Korean is a different animal to the one which arrived from Gangwon FC three years back for £2.2m.

In a recent development, haissem Hassan, Yang’s main rival on the right, hasn’t kicked a ball in Celtic’s last three matches. The fact that Forrest and Seb Tounekti stepped off the bench on Thursday before the £6m Egyptian was instructive.

According to recent reports, intriguingly, Callum Osmand remained there throughout. It won’t have escaped anyone’s notice that the 20-year-old arrived from Fulham ostensibly as a centre-forward.

He was recently afforded opportunities on the wing as Jota got back up to speed, but with the Portuguese returning to top form, that door is closing.

Osmand shouldn’t lose much sleep over that recent development, though. Without even shedding his tracksuit in Leiria, he jumped ahead of the hapless Hogh in the pecking order.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany, who finished top of Group A2 following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday are to face Belgium in the Nations League quarterfinals — after they finished second in Group A1. The Belgians recently came up with a statement result of their own, beating Italy 4-1. The match-up between the neighboring countries promises to be closely contested, with Belgium sitting at No. 8 in the men's rankings, three places above Germany.

The head coach of Belgium is former Bayern Munich player Mark van Bommel, who took over from Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual champions Spain in the quarterfinals.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.

Sources indicate that "I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he stated.

It has been revealed that "An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done.".

The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.

Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.

Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway, a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.

In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.

The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.

  • In Yizhuang, a high-tech industrial zone in Beijing, drivers have access to parts of roads, highways and intersections where they might experience green lights all the way.
  • According to recent reports, also known as the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, or Beijing E-Town, Yizhuang was created in the early 1990s by the Beijing Municipal People’s Government to act as the city’s leading smart-city demonstration zone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yizhuang, the district of Beijing where this Lingyi iTech robotics factory is located, is a key area of the city for demonstrating leading smart-city solutions.Credit: Qilai Shen/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

In Yizhuang, a high-tech industrial zone in Beijing, drivers have access to parts of roads, highways and intersections where they might experience green lights all the way. Networks of road cameras and sensors feed data to a local control centre, which issues app notifications to drivers about upcoming interruptions, recommended driving speeds and lane suggestions to keep the traffic moving. On these ‘green-wave corridors’, the average number of traffic stops throughout the day has dropped by 40.6%, and the average travel speed has increased by 15.1%, according to local reports.

According to recent reports, also known as the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, or Beijing E-Town, Yizhuang was created in the early 1990s by the Beijing Municipal People’s Government to act as the city’s leading smart-city demonstration zone. Alongside its intelligent transport systems, it has become a key area for autonomous-vehicle development and robotics, often showcasing emerging technologies at public events.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

The annual Beijing E-Town Half-Marathon, for example, attracts hundreds of humanoid robots built by companies and university teams to compete with humans over an almost 22-kilometre track. In 2025, the inaugural year of the race, many robots failed to finish. But in this year’s race, held in April, the robots showed major improvements in speed, reliability and autonomy.

Alongside Yizhuang, Beijing has many other smart-city ‘brains’ — hubs of innovation that are fast-tracking technological development in strategic areas such as artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and data governance.

One such area is Haidian in northwest Beijing, which runs a spatial-mapping platform that functions as a digital twin of the district. Gathering data from some 170,000 buildings, plus tens of thousands of road cameras and sensors, the platform flags local faults and automatically generates work orders to speed up repairs. The repair-response time for missing manhole covers, for instance, which is a major hazard for drivers and pedestrians, has been reduced from a whole day to just four hours. Haidian is home to Peking University and Tsinghua University — two of China’s leading academic institutions in the Nature Index — as well as the country’s greatest concentration of Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) institutes.

It has been revealed that underpinning Beijing’s smart-city ambitions is its enormous investment in science and technology. Beijing has been the leading science city in the Nature Index since 2016, and in 2025, its Share in the natural and health sciences was about two-thirds higher than that of its closest competitor, Shanghai. That year, Beijing spent around 6% of its gross domestic product on R&D — the highest share in the country. The city’s sprawling research system has formed close ties with its private AI sector, which, as of 2024, encompassed about 2,400 companies worth nearly 350 billion yuan (US$51.7 billion).

Recent findings suggest that A key challenge for Beijing is how to link all of the data being collected by its various districts and zones. Different departments might not feel incentivized to share their data or link up with central databases, indicates Yuan Zhibin, a senior research fellow at the CAS Institute of Science and Technology Strategy Consulting in Beijing. Strong competition between Beijing’s leading technology districts, such as Yizhuang and Haidian, as well as the costs involved in changing or updating systems, are major factors, says Yuan.

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing their core midfield for years to come.

Real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

In a recent development, both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Industry observers note that tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

His standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The fresh contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

According to recent reports, güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His latest salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

Recent findings suggest that the two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

Industry observers note that the club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The newly introduced deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

If Valverde’s extension is confirmed, none of the three midfielders would have a contract ending before 2031. That would remove contract questions over a key part of the squad for several seasons. The two completed renewals arrived during the build-up to a busy run of home matches.

The hosts thought they had taken the lead in the 14th minute. Halhal burst into the box to meet Antoine Hainaut’s whipped cross and finish into the bottom corner. However, the goal was ruled out for offside after a lengthy VAR check.

In a recent development, skorupski was the busier goalkeeper in the first half. He produced a sharp save to deny Kike Pérez’s low volley on the half-hour, then thwarted Yeboah again from inside the box shortly before the break. At the other end, Jens Odgaard fired over from a good position and Arthur Theate headed straight at Stanković.

Recent findings suggest that bologna improved after the restart, with Matteo Darmian on for Vitík. Stanković pulled off a superb reflex save to keep out Nicolò Casale’s header, and Federico Bernardeschi curled just wide from a set piece moments later.

Palladino turned to Orsolini and Nicolò Cambiaghi just before the hour, while Nicola sent on Thórir Jóhann Helgason for Busio.

It has been revealed that the chances kept coming in the closing stages. Stanković denied Lewis Ferguson’s header and then made his best save of the night to stop Tommaso Pobega from inside the six-yard box. Skorupski rushed out to smother Helgason’s effort at the other end, and Alhassane fired high and wide.

Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1392 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free.
  • On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) stated the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.
  • Recent findings suggest that look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free. Back in July 2026, DW reported how one epidemiologist had suggested an 'amnesia' about the measles risk was pushing a growth in US infections.

Four months later, it was official. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) stated the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.

But it doesn't have to stay this way.

Recent findings suggest that look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status. But within five years — during the COVID-19 pandemic — it fought and won back its measles-free status. And since 2024, Brazil has stayed measles-free, even as the highly contagious disease spread across the rest of the Americas.

Recent findings suggest that in 2026, with the data available up to the time of writing this article, Brazil had only had 70 measles cases. They were all linked to infections brought in from abroad, often from neighboring Peru.

Industry observers note that brazil has fewer people than the US, about 213 million compared to the US's nearly 350 million, but the two countries are similar in size. So the comparison is worth considering.

Brazil moves fast. The PAHO asks countries to respond within 72 hours of a suspected measles case. Here's Brazil's own rule:.

It has been revealed that it has also made hunting for cases a national habit. In a program called "Dia S," health workers knock on doors and visit schools, daycare centers and churches to find people who may be sick but have not seen a doctor.

Brazil also holds mass vaccination days called "Dia D." There was one in November, in the area where Brazil borders Colombia and Peru.

If someone is diagnosed with measles, health workers try to track down every person the patient may have met ("contact persons") and vaccinate them and other people living nearby.

The country has so far provided more than 16 million doses of the measles vaccine in 2026 and has donated 500,000 doses to Peru.

Sources indicate that brazil isn't perfect, though. According to official estimates from the World Health Organization, only 76% of children got both required doses of the vaccine in 2025 — well short of the 95% target. Experts warn this leaves the country at risk because measles is so highly contagious. A country needs to be as close to 100% immunized as possible to protect people and stop the disease from spreading.

"Elimination is not a trophy that we win once and put on a shelf. It must be protected every day," notes PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The US lost its measles-free status because the PAHO found that the same strain of the virus had been spreading in the country for 12 months or more. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status on the same day as the US.

The US has had more than 5,400 cases in 2026 (at time of writing), more than twice as many as in all of 2025, and about 19 times as many as in 2024. Nearly everyone who got sick with measles was unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

It has been revealed that US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on fresh vaccination recommendations for children in August 2026. It came at a time, when, as we reported, experts said people had stopped getting vaccinated against measles because infection rates were low. But like PAHO's Barbosa said, neglecting vaccination when infection rates are low is a mistake.

Recent findings suggest that to be fair, Trump's executive order listed the measles vaccine in a top category of vaccinations recommended for every child. But the administration's stance on vaccination in general is unclear.

Recent findings suggest that health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has often declared opposition to vaccination, including against measles, advising people to take vitamin A instead. In Texas, this led to children being hospitalized with toxic levels of the supplement, and left them with no protection against measles.

Before the COVID-19 pandemic, 95% of US kindergartners had their measles shots. Now, it's 92%, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Protection (CDC). That leaves about 280,000 kindergartners in the US unprotected.

In the Texas counties where a 2025 measles outbreak began, coverage was as low as 77% at the time.

US children usually need vaccines to start school, but most states let parents opt out for religious or personal reasons, with no doctor involved.

But vaccination rates have fallen elsewhere in the world as well, including in Europe. In Germany, where measles infections have also risen, experts blame anti-vaccination rhetoric that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic.

A person sick with measles can infect up to18 other, unprotected people. With vaccination, it is possible to increase the number of protected people and lower the number of people the sick person can infect.

Recent findings suggest that to prevent a measles outbreak, a community needs about 95% of people to be vaccinated and/or immune. The vaccination consists of two doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine.

But even after the two doses, a person can expect to have only 97% protection against measles — 3% short of full protection — so, nearly everyone in the community has to be vaccinated to keep the average level of protect as close to 100% as possible.

"For some diseases like measles, even a small decrease in vaccination rates can lead to more outbreaks of disease [so] community immunity requires over 95% of susceptible individuals to be immunized," says Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

Recent findings suggest that and the 95% has to hold everywhere. A good national average can be affected by, for example, a single school where only 70% of the children are vaccinated. And that is where the outbreak is likely to start.

Around the world, measles deaths have dropped by 88% since 2000, thanks to vaccines.

It has been revealed that but progress has stalled. Only about three out of four children worldwide get both doses of the vaccine. The biggest outbreaks right now are in Bangladesh, Indonesia and Guatemala.

Data from Europe shows that things can get better. In the European Union, cases fell from more than 35,000 in 2024 to about 2,300 the following year, with no measles-related deaths.

Romania went from more than 30,000 cases in 2024 to about 4,200 in 2025.

In Hungary, where 99% of children are vaccinated, there have been no measles cases in the past year.

Industry observers note that but in January, six European countries lost their measles-free status, including the UK, Spain and Austria. Across Europe, eight out of ten people who got measles in 2025 were unvaccinated.

The Americas are seeing a major surge in measles infections, with more than 58,000 cases in 2026, over four times as many as by November in 2025. Guatemala has been hit hardest, with almost 35,000 cases.

The deadliest outbreaks are in Africa. African Union countries have so far reported nearly 1,800 measles deaths in 2026, about 1,650 of them in Democratic Republic of Congo. Yet, Sudan, despite the war, raised first-dose measles coverage by 22 percentage points in 2025, which was the world's largest gain.

In a recent development, measles is extremely contagious. One person can infect up to 18 unprotected people, which makes it about 12 times more contagious than the flu.

In a recent development, the virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after a sick person has left the room. And people spread it before they know they are sick. Someone with measles is contagious for four days before the rash appears and four days after.

Industry observers note that it's not just a rash. About one in five unvaccinated people who get measles in the US ends up in the hospital. Measles can weaken the immune system for years, making it harder to fight off other infections.

But it's preventable. Two doses of the MMR vaccine (which also protects against mumps and rubella) protect 97% of people for life.

Latest Update: Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2299 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life.
  • We are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions.
  • Industry observers note that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life. A 10-game sample size -- that's the useful stuff. At this point, many but not all teams are what their analytics tell us they are. It's similar but not quite the same for players. Not many have hit the 900-minute mark yet, but plenty are at 500-plus, a body of evidence that usually isn't warped by any one good or bad game. Of course, it depends on how good or bad that game is.

We are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions. We are, however, in a position to find some interesting questions. Here are five of them, in player form:.

Industry observers note that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running. That's especially true when they're Bruno Guimaraes, terror of Premier League midfields in a Newcastle United shirt, a player who had long since seemed ready to step up to a Champions League contender. While it would be fair to say that the Brazilian's form is nothing like a problem for table-topping Arsenal, he has not exactly started like a house on fire. Mikel Arteta has acknowledged as much whenever he has spoken about Guimaraes, even when served up the opportunity to praise him after what seemed an impressive performance against Hull City.

"He's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room -- he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come." It would be fair to say that, Hull aside, the best levels he has hit have been as a substitute. When he comes off the bench, he passes more accurately, wins more tackles, creates chances and scores brilliant goals. As a starter, he has occasionally looked a beat off his teammates.

Industry observers note that physical data from Gradient Sports hints as to what the matter might be. For every 90 Premier League minutes on the field, Guimaraes covers less of it at sprint speed (≥25 km/h) than any outfield player bar Mikel Merino and spends notably more time jogging than anyone, an average of 30 minutes. Compare Guimaraes to Declan Rice, an admittedly vertiginous bar, and it is easy to see why the upcoming guy looks off the pace.

Recent findings suggest that equally, it explains why he's such a compelling substitute. When the other 21 players on the pitch are flagging, Guimaraes' comparative physical problems go unexposed and he can run the show.

In a recent development, that's all well and good for now, but he can't carry on like this, can he? You would have to assume that Myles Lewis-Skelly will have to make way even if the academy graduate's emergence as a midfield option unlocked an improved Declan Rice at the tail end of last season. The second most expensive signing in your history can't be an impact guy off the bench behind the homegrown kid, right? Probably not, but if there's any team that could justify the idea of Guimaraes as a 12th man, maybe it's Arsenal, where they pride themselves on their game-changing finishers.

Erling Haaland's Swiftian reign at the top of the Premier League xG chart has been interrupted, at least temporarily, by an unlikely source. You'd have to go back to the days of a marauding Romelu Lukaku for the last time an Everton striker looked like they might rule the roost. Only once since the Belgian's departure has an Evertonian cleared 20 goals in all competitions. In the last five, even a dozen has been beyond this club.

Sources indicate that thierno Barry isn't there yet, but boy is he on the right trajectory. His 7.28 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) puts him 0.22 ahead of Haaland and nearly 2.5 npxG up on anyone else in the league. Expand the pool to Europe's top five leagues and he is breathing rarefied air behind the top four of Lamine Yamal, Donyell Malen, Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe, all of whom have the advantage that they are not playing for an upper midtable outfit in the continent's most competitive division. And in that environment, Barry is making the hardest thing in the sport look easy: getting good shots in prime locations.

According to recent reports, if Barry were turning them in as often as he was getting them, Everton might be even higher than sixth. Still, six goals through 10 games is not to be sniffed at, particularly when the pressure on the 24-year-old was so intense. The bungling of a deadline-day move for Folarin Balogun, as Beto moved to Fiorentina, meant it was Barry or bust for David Moyes this season.

Industry observers note that perhaps it was an enforced show of faith for a player who was in and out of the XI last season, his first in England, that brought the best out of the former Villarreal man. His manager views the success in more straightforward terms. "He has settled down a bit more," mentioned Moyes after Barry's brace helped down Coventry. "His language, his understanding, his communication is much better and he has worked hard to get himself in those positions to score.".

It is easy to see why getting the soft factors right might have been all that was required. Barry is the ideal striker for the modern Premier League. Tall, strong and mobile -- he ranks third among center forwards for top speed this season, per Gradient Sports -- he can serve as an outball when a press needs beating and then get in the box. He might not have the technical elegance of an Mbappe, but he makes his presence felt and occupies high-value spaces. That is more valuable than it sounds, as proven when James Tarkowski's howitzer from range deflected in off him. You might not like it, but this is what elite center forward play looks like. Long may it continue, at least as far as Everton are concerned.

There are three types of underrated footballers. First, your common-or-garden-variety underrated footballers, often to be found plying their trade at Wolverhampton Wanderers or Burnley. Ashley Westwood, in that season, put up stupidly high xA numbers. Then there are the so-often-dubbed-underrated that they actually become a bit overrated. Leighton Baines. Lee Carsley. They don't have to play for Everton, but it does help. Olivier Giroud is another. See, not all Everton.

It has been revealed that the most rarely spotted of the underrated is the chameleonic one, correctly pegged for a while, only to develop to the point that he is underrated in a completely different way to how he once was. Take Alex Iwobi. Some time ago, a consensus coalesced around the Nigeria international that he was a good player for a team at Fulham's level (and indeed Everton's). Any minute he was on the field, he would probably be delivering good performances for good Premier League teams.

In a recent development, not anymore. Ten games in and Iwobi looks like one of the outstanding creative forces in the Premier League, critical to the march towards adequacy that Fulham have undertaken after a slow start to life with Alvaro Arbeloa.

Among true playmakers, Iwobi is one of the best at getting the ball into dangerous areas and creating for his teammates. Iwobi leads the league in expected assists with 2.95 and is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area. Only Pascal Gross has created more chances.

According to recent reports, those players can't match Iwobi when it comes to ball progression either. In terms of advancing the ball not just into the box but from deeper, Fulham's ball-playing fulcrum on the inside left channel has completed more progressive passes than anyone not named Declan Rice or Jan Paul van Hecke.

When Iwobi broke through at Arsenal, he displayed a preternatural sense for how to keep attacks alive, the pass before the pass before the pass. Now a 30-year-old, Iwobi still does that more than he unpicks defenses. One cannot argue, however, that he is not putting his teammates in the right spot. It is just that not everyone quite appreciates how often he does so just yet, including his own supporters, who jeered Iwobi when he was substituted in the early-season defeat to Crystal Palace. Since then, he has responded to his critics in style, teeing up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven Premier League matches. If a few more of them had been converted, in fact, if any of them had been converted, then Iwobi might not still be underrated.

Industry observers note that the upper reaches of the list of most expensive transfers of all time are hardly all bangers all the time, but of the biggest money moves in the sport's history there are only a handful where at such an early stage you find yourself wondering if anyone really understood what the plan was. Manchester City committed the best part of $150 million on Enzo Fernandez this summer, a fee only eclipsed by Neymar and Kylian Mbappe. Beyond a vague sense that it would be nice to give new manager Enzo Maresca one of his favorite players, what was it they had in mind?

We pointed out earlier in the season that the aggressive positioning of Fernandez in the 5-3 win over Sunderland looked extreme; at the time it seemed reasonable to view it as a reflection of a stretched-out, chaotic game. Maresca had, of course, unlocked more number 10-ish qualities in the Argentine at Chelsea, but surely that had been reflective of what that team needed, particularly as Cole Palmer went off the boil? Perhaps not. Fernandez keeps popping up in the sort of positions that leave Elliot Anderson on an island. It is one thing to view Anderson as the new Rodri, quite another to immediately throw the England international in at the deep end, tying a whole midfield together by force of will.

Sources indicate that of course you could sketch out a logic for why you might push Fernandez high. It is not so long ago that City deployed two playmakers in front of a sitting midfielder and they ruled the Premier League. Fernandez and Rayan Cherki aren't Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva though.

It has been revealed that maybe Cherki could be offering a level of creation on a par with City greats; he started well enough last season. In year two, he is creating lower-quality chances, his expected assists per 90 dropping by 50%, notably more than the slight uptick in the quality and quantity of shots he is taking. It's no surprise that Cherki is creating less when fewer of his touches are coming in the attacking third. The output has been there so far, five goals and two assists in nine Premier League games, but for that to continue, Maresca might want to be getting his No. 10 into more dangerous spots.

Industry observers note that instead, those seem to be going to Fernandez, who has not proven himself able to get the final-third production to justify his platforming. For every 100 touches he takes, he is delivering significantly less npxG+xA than in either of the previous two seasons. Meanwhile, he is less effective without the ball than he has been at any stage since coming to England. That's no wonder. If an opponent passes through City's frontline, then Fernandez does not have the mobility to get back.

Sources indicate that as such, to enable themselves to get perhaps a shot or two more than they would get with Ayyoub Bouaddi or Mateo Kovacic next to Anderson, City have made themselves an even more vulnerable side to the counterattack, already giving up more fast-break openings than they did in 2020-21 or 2021-22. Carry on like this, and Fernandez will become one of those nine-figure transfers, the ones that live in infamy.

Recent findings suggest that it was a signing that delighted a city when it was unveiled in early August, and rightly so. Loaning Carl Rushworth from Brighton had been an inspired bit of business by Coventry City, the then-24-year-old goalkeeper anchoring the best defense in the division as Frank Lampard's side returned to the top flight for the first time in over a quarter of a century. A club-record £22 million fee seemed a snip for such a young talent.

Industry observers note that all of that is worth bearing in mind given the struggles Rushworth has endured this season: saving just 53.7% of shots he has faced, conceding 5.19 more goals than the xG value of the shots he has faced. The swagger of last season has been replaced by a sloppiness apparent in both the goals he conceded in the second half against Tottenham, weak gloves doing nothing to repel efforts that came at him a bit quicker and a bit sooner than they might have last year.

None of this needs to be a problem for Rushworth. In 2023-24, James Trafford was another highly touted young goalkeeper afforded a shot at the significant time by Burnley. He was obliterated up and down the Premier League, his first touch in the division picking the ball out of the net off Erling Haaland. Those struggles were the making of him, as they have broken others. It'll be some time yet before we discover which way these past few months send Rushworth.

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 17:29 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 27 November 2026.

It is not yet December and already chaos threatens to engulf Chelsea once more.

A bright start to the season under Xabi Alonso was, it transpires, merely a hazy, late summer mirage. Winter, it seems, will bring only a fresh version of a classic modern Chelsea discontent.

A coach who has started to do strange things – Alonso selected midfielder Moises Caicedo at centre-half here for the first time in his seven-year club career – a fanbase turning on everyone from the owners to the players and a team slowly getting disorientated on a dismally familiar carousel of selection changes.

In a recent development, it is Chelsea rebooted but just with the same stories written by and for different people. How dismal it must feel for those with this great club in their hearts.

Here on a misty and rainy night at the City Ground, nobody suffered more in Chelsea colours than central defender Wesley Fofana.

Harangued throughout by his own travelling fans for a foolish and unauthorised midweek YouTube interview in which he seemed to make light of missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool, the Frenchman was hauled off soon after conceding a penalty that allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to stretch Nottingham Forest’s lead to two goals early in the second half.

Wesley Fofana was hauled off soon after conceding a penalty that allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to stretch Nottingham Forest’s lead to two goals early in the second half.

Fofana was harangued throughout by his own travelling fans for an unauthorised interview in which he seemed to make light of missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You are not wanted here,’ sang the Chelsea fans and after this they may get their wish. For his own sake, it may be a while before we see the young defender again.

Sources indicate that at that stage of the night, Chelsea actually still had hope. Half-time substitute Emmanuel Emegha had just pulled a goal back with his team’s first shot on target of the whole night. He was to get another right at the death, too.

But having started the game with a fabulous fifth minute volley from the Brazilian Igor Jesus – it came off his shin but that doesn’t matter – Forest had the look of a team with their opponents’ measure all evening and that was how it played out. And when Gibbs-White scored his second of the game to make it 3-1 with less than 20 minutes left, Chelsea’s night was pretty much over.

Recent findings suggest that alonso must certainly take his share of the blame here. Caicedo is his best midfielder but was played out of position with England’s Levi Colwill left on the bench.

In a recent development, put simply, it backfired. Chelsea’s defending did not improve on recent efforts and in midfield, where they were outplayed by Forest’s Xaver Schlager and James McAtee, they missed the Ecuadorian desperately.

According to recent reports, more widely Alonso’s Premier League record – six wins from 12 games – is now worse than that of Liam Rosenior when he was sacked back in April. Their six defeats are one more than Manchester United. And this at a time when Chelsea are playing but once a week. No European competition and out of the Carabao Cup, the Spaniard has plenty of time with his players on the training field. What is he doing with it? Confusing everybody, it would seem, for what Chelsea presented here was a jumble. How they lost by only a goal was a miracle in itself. They deserved nothing.

Sources indicate that forest had come in to the game with issues of their own. Their coach Oliver Glasner had accused his international squad of not making enough effort with their English. Early on their football spoke for them as McAtee spread the play with a wonderful fifth minute pass, Daniel Munoz crossed and Jesus rose to volley his second league goal of the season high past Emiliano Martinez quite wonderfully.

Caicedo is Alonso's best midfielder but the Ecuadorian was played out of position by the Chelsea manager with England’s Levi Colwill left on the bench.

Alonso’s Premier League record – six wins from 12 games – is now worse than that of Liam Rosenior when he was sacked back in April.

What followed for the rest of the first half did not match that quality. Over time, Alonso’s team did find a way into the game territorially but a free-kick routine that ended with Morgan Rogers ballooning ten yards over the bar perhaps summed their efforts up as indeed did the fact they ended the opening period having managed only three touches inside the Forest box.

Sources indicate that replacing the ineffectual Danny Welbeck with Emegha at the interval brought Chelsea some shape at least. Welbeck had been peripheral. Forest were the team to kick on, though, and when Fofana slipped catastrophically to allow Liam Delap through in the 50th minute, he then brought him down. Gibbs-White slotted in the penalty and Chelsea were in substantial trouble.

Recent findings suggest that with the away end threatening revolt, Alonso’s team somehow fashioned a lifeline goal from nowhere within four minutes. Pedro Neto’s speculative shot struck Forest defender Jair Cunha on the thigh and when the ball dropped to Emegha, he controlled it instinctively and found the corner.

With Fofana soon withdrawn to doubtless protect his own sanity, Chelsea’s fans now had nothing else to do but support their team. The visitors’ sense of desperation certainly made it a better game but what followed only served to damn Chelsea even more.

Far from the goal imbuing them with the impetus and belief to rescue the game, Alonso’s players somehow allowed Forest to take the initiative once more. There was a fatuous and unsuccessful penalty appeal for handball against Cunha – he had his arms clamped to his side when Rogers’ cross struck him – but precious little else.

And when the generally excellent Austrian Schlager threaded the needle to find Gibbs-White through a crowd with 17 minutes left, the England forward lifted the ball over the advancing Martinez to present a two-goal margin once again.

Chelsea subsequently offered almost nothing only to score – this time with an Emegha header – with two minutes left. Had they added an equaliser it would have been wholly unjust. They didn’t.

Substitute Carlos Espí struck late as Real Madrid came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu. The result keeps Madrid firmly in the title race with Barcelona.

The victory over Celta on Saturday 21 November 2026 was Madrid’s ninth in a row. It also kept their 100% home record this season intact.

The winner began with a Vinícius Júnior cross. Espí headed it, Celta goalkeeper Ionuț Radu saved, and the striker scored from the rebound in the six-yard box. He had been on the pitch for only a few minutes.

Industry observers note that espí had played only 44 minutes of LaLiga football this season before kick-off, according to ESPN. All three of his league goals have now won games, against Espanyol, Elche and Celta. He also scored in the 4-3 Champions League comeback win at Roma. The goal was his fourth of the season, the club remarked.

Sources indicate that espí called his first goal in front of the Bernabéu crowd his most special for the club. José Mourinho described him as a pure penalty-box striker. The coach added that football history has many players like him who decide games without playing many minutes.

Pablo Durán gave Celta a sixth-minute lead from a Williot Swedberg pass. Kylian Mbappé then missed a penalty in the 39th minute, and the visitors led 1-0 at the break.

Mourinho had started Vinícius and Federico Valverde on the bench. He sent them on with Marc Cucurella in the second half to chase the game. Thibaut Courtois kept Madrid in it with a strong low save from a long-range Durán shot in the 65th minute. A minute later, Jude Bellingham equalised from an Mbappé assist.

Sources indicate that the figures show how one-sided the contest was. Madrid had 24 shots to Celta’s 8 and an expected goals total of 3.8 against 1.52. Radu made five saves, and the hosts held 64% of possession.

Celta coach Claudio Giráldez remarked Madrid’s substitutes had decided the game. He pointed out that he had started six academy graduates. Many of his players were appearing at the Bernabéu for the first time. Giráldez replaced Hugo Álvarez with Ferran Jutglà at half-time and sent on Iago Aspas for Durán in the 76th minute. Celta are 13th on 13 points.

Barcelona still top the table on goal difference, 35 to 22. They can move clear again when they host Villarreal on Sunday 22 November.

In the LaLiga scoring chart, Mbappé is second with 13 goals. Barcelona’s Raphinha leads on 15.

Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2244 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that UPCOMING YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune noted post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • Sources indicate that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that UPCOMING YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune noted post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Sources indicate that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game blueprint that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during New York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

"We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins mentioned. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

It has been revealed that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness issues over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

It has been revealed that "I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill remarked. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Industry observers note that gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of New York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

In the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

Sources indicate that "As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match plan that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

The Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a blueprint," Armas remarked. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while right now headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

Recent findings suggest that "Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros noted. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up blueprint for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Newly introduced York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce said. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

Industry observers note that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

"I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

Sources indicate that "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it is becoming increasingly difficult for young people in Germany to find a job after finishing university or professional training.
  • According to recent reports, furthermore, young people do not feel that politicians are taking action on concerns that matter to them, such as climate protection.
  • What particularly infuriates many young people is being talked about rather than spoken to.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it is becoming increasingly difficult for young people in Germany to find a job after finishing university or professional training. And finding an affordable place to live in a big city, and finally starting to live independently is becoming almost impossible.

According to recent reports, furthermore, young people do not feel that politicians are taking action on concerns that matter to them, such as climate protection. The climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, is a case in point. It, therefore, shouldn't be a surprise that young people across Europe once again took to the streets this Friday, which was World Children's Day too, to make their voices heard. In Germany, Gen Z protests took place in 73 towns and cities.

What particularly infuriates many young people is being talked about rather than spoken to. Equally infuriating is seeing their protests branded as criminal before they have even begun, all because of the actions of a small minority.

One example of such rhetoric was when the youth wing of the conservative Christian Democratic Union/Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) party in Berlin-Mitte suggested deploying the German army against demonstrations.

It can also be seen in the media, such as when Bild, Germany's highest-circulation tabloid, ran a headline that translated as: "Young, male, known to the police — who rioted after the demonstrations and where chaos threatens today.".

In a recent development, "Young people are taking to the streets because they feel they are not being heard. And, of course, that feeling is strongly reinforced when the press devotes no more than a brief paragraph to their demands while focusing the rest of its coverage on how these protests could become problematic," states Erik Sczygiol, who until recently was deputy secretary-general of the Federal Conference of Student Representatives. "Of course, any potential security concerns need to be addressed, but they should not overshadow media coverage of the protests.".

The 18-year-old Sczygiol is almost an exception. He was invited to participate in the launch of the World Population Report in Bonn alongside representatives of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the German Foundation for World Population (DSW). This year's report, entitled "Succeeding Generations: Empowering young people to chart the future," is particularly noteworthy because it focuses on Gen Z.

According to recent reports, UN researchers surveyed 109,000 people across 73 countries for the report, some of whose findings are encouraging. Young people worldwide are better educated than any generation before them, with 78% of adolescents across the globe completing at least lower secondary education. But finding a job is becoming increasingly difficult, while informal employment is on the rise.

Industry observers note that this economic uncertainty has far-reaching consequences for young people. According to the report, people often do not achieve financial independence until they are in their mid-to-late 20s, and a stable partnership and parenthood are often not realities before their early-to-mid 30s.

Nor do young people have a seat at the political decision-making table when it comes to shaping future reforms in the labor market, housing or climate protection. Florian Brod, 25, points out: "Almost half of the world's population is under 30, yet only 2.6% of parliamentarians worldwide are under 30.".

According to recent reports, young people need and want change to protect their livelihoods and those of future generations. "Yet those who will have to live longest with the consequences of today's decisions are precisely the ones who have hardly any representation in the political decision-making process," notes Brod.

He is somewhat close to the political decision-making process as he has served as a Youth Delegate for Sustainable Development for almost two years. In this role, he represents the interests of young people in Germany at United Nations conferences. This is certainly an important step towards giving his generation a greater say in political processes.

Nevertheless, both Brod and Sczygiol have had similar experiences. They often participate in conferences and panel discussions and are invited to submit their opinions, but these invitations often amount to little more than symbolic gestures.

In a recent development, "Having access to an international conference is a first step. But without substantive briefings ahead of the conference, without involvement in preliminary negotiations and, in some cases, without access to negotiation texts, there is little opportunity for us to help shape the outcome. When young people see their demands making little headway politically while they are simultaneously excluded from the search for solutions, frustration inevitably builds," indicates Brod.

Sczygiol adds: "We often get the feeling at the Federal Youth Conference that we were invited simply to provide a nice photo opportunity. We may be sitting at the table, but often only once a bill has already gone through 17 different drafts and is just days away from its final vote in the Bundestag. By that stage, young people have virtually no say in changing anything, and their voices are barely heard. Their contributions are often simply dismissed with: 'Well, that's just typical youthful nonsense.' And that is something that really frustrates young people.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, medical student Amelie Belosevic knows that feeling all too well. She served as Germany's Youth Delegate at the World Health Assembly in Geneva in May. Twenty-five countries sent youth representatives, which Belosevic sees as a clear step forward. However, she has one criticism. According to the United Nations Population Fund, 90% of the world's 1.8 billion young people live in the Global South. Yet, the region was represented by only eight delegates. As a result, Africa, Latin America and large parts of Asia were left virtually voiceless.

Industry observers note that her demands for Germany include better job prospects for young people entering the workforce and sustainable pension systems 40 years from now. "For a very long time, people have remarked 'I believe my children will have a better life than I do.' But that is no longer necessarily true. So it makes sense then that those who feel the greatest anxiety about the future are the people who have most of their life ahead of them. Sometimes, people don't understand that. We young people need to be able to believe in our future again!".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S.
  • After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • Recent findings suggest that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that says it's not key tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his intends for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

"What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino stated. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

Sources indicate that for all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an notable new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

As for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his new role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

It has been revealed that two years removed from starting a fresh job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-key clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

It has been revealed that "For me, it's not difficult," he said of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most key [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

Diego Kochen shows poise in USMNT net as young goalkeeper stakes claim to starting job

💡 Key Takeaways
